# Swift Pieces: full text

> 55 free SwiftUI components for iOS, one Swift file each, MIT + Commons Clause. Index: https://swiftpieces.com/llms.txt. Source for any piece: https://swiftpieces.com/r/<Name>.json or its docs page.

# Components

## Assistant Orb (`AssistantOrb`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/ai/assistant-orb
Category: AI. iOS 17.0+. Metal shader.
Files: AssistantOrb.swift, AssistantOrb.metal
Install: npx swiftpieces add AssistantOrb

A dark glass ball with a Siri-style voice wave inside, locked to the thinking state; four thin sine membranes travel through the equator of a refracting shell, drawn by a Metal color shader. The sphere never moves, only the wave, and a palette change crossfades its colours.

The assistant's mark while it thinks. Copy `AssistantOrb.metal` alongside this file; its `assistantOrbSiriWave` kernel compiles into your app's default Metal library.

### Notes

- Requires `AssistantOrb.metal` in the same target. The `[[ stitchable ]] assistantOrbSiriWave` function is looked up through `ShaderLibrary` at runtime. Its helpers live in the `assistantOrbSiri` namespace, so it can share a target with other orb kernels.
- The orb has one look: thinking. Four thin sine membranes in blue, pink, orange and red travel left to right through the equator over a violet ground, seen through a refracting glass shell with a cool and warm rim. There is no idle or speaking phase, no audio level and no touch interaction. Colour is the only input: `palette` defaults to `.siri`, and `AssistantOrb.Palette(bands:ground:crest:rimCool:rimWarm:)` takes hex values or `Color`s for your brand. A palette change crossfades all eight colours over 0.8s (instantly under Reduce Motion); the motion never changes.
- The sphere never scales, floats or pulses; only the wave inside it moves. Put the orb on a dark surface and pair it with your own status copy if the step changes.
- `size` sets a square frame. The ball fills 90% of it, so leave the frame square.
- The clock is relative to first appearance so `Float` precision holds over long sessions. Reduce Motion pauses the timeline on a still frame. VoiceOver reads "Assistant" with "Thinking" as its value.

### Parameters

- `size`: Diameter of the ball in points. 160 by default; the view is always a square of this side.
- `palette`: The eight colours of the wave, ground, crest and rim. `.siri` by default; build your own with `Palette(bands:ground:crest:rimCool:rimWarm:)` from hex or `Color`. A change crossfades over 0.8s.

## Code Block (`CodeBlock`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/ai/code-block
Category: AI. iOS 17.0+.
Files: CodeBlock.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add CodeBlock

A code slab for chat replies and docs that stays dark in both appearances: a butter language label and optional filename, block-colored Swift syntax, collapse past N lines with a fade and a spring expand, wrap toggle, text selection, a streaming mode that fades lines in behind a cursor, and a copy pill that turns into a sage Copied block.

Code block with a tiny Swift scanner. Keywords, types, strings and numbers take block colors on a dark slab; comments and punctuation recede.

### Notes

- The slab stays dark in both appearances (ink `#141414` on paper, charcoal on the dark ground) so block-colored syntax always reads. The header carries a butter language label, an optional `title` filename, a wrap toggle and a Copy pill.
- Highlighting is a small hand-written scanner for Swift only: keywords, `@attributes` and `#directives` are bold tangerine, capitalized types are sky, string literals (including `"""` blocks) are sage, numbers are lilac, and comments and punctuation recede. Other languages render plain.
- Blocks longer than `collapseAfter` + 2 lines show the first `collapseAfter` lines under a fade and a "Show N more lines" pill; expanding is a spring. Collapse is skipped while `isStreaming`.
- The wrap toggle switches the scroll axes between `.horizontal` and none, so the same `Text` views wrap or scroll without re-creating the view. It fills in when on.
- With `isStreaming`, appended lines fade in over 0.25s and a tangerine cap-height capsule trails the last line. Copy writes to `UIPasteboard`, turns the pill into a sage Copied block for 1.6s, and fires a success haptic.
- `Style` (`CodeBlock.Style`): `slab`, `raised`, `text`, `muted`, `gutter`, `ink`, `label`, `keyword`, `string`, `type`, `number`, `copied`, `cornerRadius`. `accent:` still overrides the string and copied colors.
- Text selection is enabled on the code column; `.footnote` monospaced scales with Dynamic Type.
- Need code inside fully rendered streaming markdown? That is the Streaming Markdown screen in Swift Pieces Pro.

### Parameters

- `code`: Source text. Newlines split it into lines. Append while `isStreaming` to fade new lines in.
- `language`: Label in the header; highlighting applies only when it is "swift".
- `showsLineNumbers`: Show a right-aligned gutter.
- `collapseAfter`: Collapse blocks longer than this many lines behind a fade and a "Show more" control. `nil` never collapses.
- `wrapsLines`: Initial wrap state. The header toggle flips it at runtime.
- `isStreaming`: Appended lines fade in and a cursor sits after the last line.
- `accent`: Color for string literals and the copied state. `nil` uses `style.string` and `style.copied`.
- `title`: Optional filename shown beside the language label, such as "Greeter.swift".
- `style`: Slab, text and syntax colors and corner radius. Defaults to the house palette.

## Prompt Chips (`PromptChips`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/ai/prompt-chips
Category: AI. iOS 17.0+.
Files: PromptChips.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add PromptChips

A snapping horizontal row of prompt suggestions above a composer, each chip keyed by a solid color block glyph. The chosen chip morphs into a composer-width block with matchedGeometryEffect while the rest slide out, then the row hands the text back and collapses.

Prompt suggestions in a horizontally snapping row, sized for thumb reach directly above a composer.

### Notes

- Each chip is a soft card with a 32pt solid color glyph block on its leading edge; `style.blocks` cycle across chips (tangerine, sky, butter, sage, lilac) and `symbols:` gives each chip its own glyph. Pass `tint` for a single color.
- The row is a horizontal `ScrollView` with `viewAligned` snapping and 16pt content margins; shadows are not clipped (`scrollClipDisabled`). Chips reveal with a staggered spring. Place the row directly above the composer.
- Selection is a two-step `matchedGeometryEffect`: a composer-width block in the chip's color is inserted at the chip's frame, then one frame later released to its own frame with a spring while the other chips slide 32pt outward and fade. `onSelect` fires when it lands (about 0.45s) and the row collapses to zero height, so put the text in your composer and remove or `.id()` the row.
- Press feel is 0.96 with a fast ease in, a bouncy spring out, and one soft impact per press; choosing adds a selection haptic.
- `Style` (`PromptChips.Style`): `blocks`, `surface`, `text`, `ink`, `cornerRadius`.
- Under Reduce Motion there is no morph: the row crossfades and collapses in 0.2s.
- Need a full composer with attachments, recording and model picker? That is the Prompt Composer screen in Swift Pieces Pro.

### Parameters

- `suggestions`: Chip titles, in order.
- `systemImage`: Glyph on every chip's color block. Pass `nil` for text-only chips.
- `symbols`: Optional per-chip glyphs, matched to `suggestions` by index. Falls back to `systemImage`.
- `tint`: One block color for every chip and the morph target. `nil` cycles `style.blocks`.
- `style`: Chip surface, text, block colors and radius. Defaults to the house palette.
- `selection`: Optional two-way selection. Set it to a suggestion to choose it programmatically; the row writes the chosen title back when it lands.
- `onSelect`: Called with the chosen title once the morph lands (about 0.45 s; 0.2 s under Reduce Motion).

## Streaming Reply (`StreamingReply`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/ai/streaming-reply
Category: AI. iOS 17.0+.
Files: StreamingReply.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add StreamingReply

The AI reply surface. A small header carries the assistant mark and a live phase label, text arrives token by token with a per-word fade and a color block cursor, inline code sits on butter blocks, user prompts are solid color blocks, and a long press lifts the message to reveal copy and regenerate.

A chat message that streams. Assistant replies sit on the ground under a mark and phase label; user messages are a solid color block.

### Notes

- Assistant replies sit on the ground under a header: a 24pt ink mark, the name (`style.assistantName`) and a small uppercase phase label (THINKING, WRITING, STOPPED). User prompts are a solid block (`style.userBlock`, sky) with dark ink and a tucked bottom-trailing corner. Set `style.showsHeader = false` for a bare reply.
- Text is split into word tokens (each word keeps its trailing whitespace). On iOS 18 a private `TextRenderer` draws each token at its own fade-in opacity with a 2pt rise; on iOS 17 the same opacities are written into the `AttributedString` runs. Only words that arrive after the view appears animate, so loaded history renders instantly.
- Inline markdown renders; inline `code` sits on a butter block with dark ink.
- The cursor is an inline tangerine capsule sized from the body font's cap height, so it flows with the text and scales with Dynamic Type. On iOS 18 it pulses through the renderer; on iOS 17 it is solid.
- `phase` is a value, not internal state: drive `.thinking` (block-colored rising dots and a pulsing mark), `.streaming`, `.done`, `.error(message)` from your stream. `.error` turns the mark signal and shows the message with a signal Retry pill that calls `onAction(.regenerate)`.
- Long press (0.35s) lifts the message onto a card with a rigid impact and shows a solid ink capsule with Copy and Regenerate. Copy writes to `UIPasteboard`, morphs to Copied with a success haptic, then sets the message down. Tap the message to put it down.
- `Style` (`StreamingReply.Style`): `userBlock`, `cursor`, `code`, `dots`, `signal`, `ink`, `text`, `muted`, `surface`, `mark`, `markInk`, `actionFill`, `actionInk`, `assistantName`, `showsHeader`. `tint:` still overrides the user block and cursor.
- Under Reduce Motion tokens appear without fading, the cursor and mark hold still, and the lift is a 0.15s ease.
- Need full incremental markdown with lists, tables, source cards and a follow-up bar? That is the Streaming Markdown screen in Swift Pieces Pro.

### Parameters

- `text`: The message body. Append to it as tokens arrive; each new word fades in. Inline markdown is rendered.
- `role`: `.assistant` (leading, header and open text) or `.user` (trailing, solid block).
- `phase`: `.thinking` shows dots, `.streaming` shows the cursor, `.done` settles, `.error` shows the message and a retry.
- `tint`: Block color for user messages and the streaming cursor. `nil` uses `style.userBlock` and `style.cursor`.
- `fadeDuration`: Seconds each new word takes to fade in.
- `style`: Colors, the assistant name and whether the header shows. Defaults to the house palette.
- `onAction`: Called with `.copy` or `.regenerate` from the long-press actions or the error retry.

## Thinking State (`ThinkingState`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/ai/thinking-state
Category: AI. iOS 17.0+.
Files: ThinkingState.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add ThinkingState

The "assistant is working" placeholder, laid out like the reply it becomes: a breathing mark with an elapsed-seconds label over three presentations on one clock: block-colored rising dots, a sheen over reply-shaped bars, or a label whose glyphs carry the sheen. Plus a modifier that sweeps any view.

Placeholder for a reply that has not started. Every presentation mirrors the `StreamingReply` layout (mark and label, then content) so it resolves into the real message without a layout jump.

### Notes

- Every presentation shares the `StreamingReply` layout: a header (breathing ink mark, name and a THINKING · 3S elapsed label that counts up) and then content sized to a body line, so swapping `ThinkingState` for a `StreamingReply` does not shift anything. Set `style.showsHeader = false` for content only.
- `.dots` rises three block-colored dots (tangerine, sky, lilac by default), `.sheen` sweeps a band across reply-shaped bars, and `.text(label)` sweeps the band through the label's glyphs.
- One `TimelineView` drives the mark's breath, the dots and the sheen, so they stay phase-locked. `duration` sets the sweep period.
- Pass `tint` to use one color for the dots, mark and sheen.
- `.thinkingState(_:tint:)` masks a bright sweep to the view's own alpha, so it follows capsules, glyphs and text with no clipping setup, and fades out when `isActive` turns false. It reads best on solid blocks.
- `Style` (`ThinkingState.Style`): `dots`, `bar`, `sheen`, `mark`, `markInk`, `ink`, `text`, `muted`, `assistantName`, `showsHeader`.
- Under Reduce Motion the clock holds still: the band sits mid-view, the dots rest and the mark keeps a steady size; only the elapsed seconds update.
- Need a live timeline of tool calls with durations and results? That is the Tool Execution Card screen in Swift Pieces Pro.

### Parameters

- `presentation`: `.dots`, `.sheen` (reply-shaped bars), or `.text(label)`.
- `tint`: Optional single color for the dots, mark and sheen. `nil` uses the house blocks for the dots and a neutral sheen.
- `lineCount`: Number of placeholder bars in the `.sheen` presentation.
- `duration`: Seconds per sheen sweep; the dots and mark breathe on the same clock.
- `style`: Colors, the assistant name and whether the header with elapsed seconds shows. Defaults to the house palette.

## Thought Orb (`ThoughtOrb`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/ai/thought-orb
Category: AI. iOS 17.0+. Metal shader.
Files: ThoughtOrb.swift, ThoughtOrb.metal
Install: npx swiftpieces add ThoughtOrb

A small dark glass ball with a Siri-style voice wave inside, locked to the thinking state and drawn by a Metal color shader; palettes for searching, reading and writing crossfade the colour with the kind of work, and a Pill wraps it with a label and indeterminate dots into the status control.

The mark next to the verb an agent is doing. Copy `ThoughtOrb.metal` alongside this file; its `thoughtOrbSiriWave` kernel compiles into your app's default Metal library.

### Notes

- Requires `ThoughtOrb.metal` in the same target. The `[[ stitchable ]] thoughtOrbSiriWave` function is looked up through `ShaderLibrary` at runtime. Its helpers live in the `thoughtOrbSiri` namespace, so it can share a target with other orb kernels.
- The mark has one look: thinking. Four thin sine membranes travel left to right through the equator of a dark glass ball. There are no motion states and no drag; the sphere never scales or pulses, only the wave inside it moves.
- Colour says what kind of work is happening. Presets: `.siri` for thinking (blue, pink, orange, red over violet), `.searching` (cyan into teal), `.reading` (lavender into indigo) and `.writing` (amber into coral). Build your own with `ThoughtOrb.Palette(bands:ground:crest:rimCool:rimWarm:)`. A change crossfades over 0.8s, instantly under Reduce Motion.
- Drive it from the current step: `ThoughtOrb.Pill(step.title, palette: step.palette)` changes the label with a numeric text transition and crossfades the mark to the step's colour, while the motion keeps thinking. `ThoughtOrb(size: 64)` works at avatar size.
- `Pill` derives type, padding and dots from `markSize` (0.47x label, 0.2x padding) and scales the whole thing with Dynamic Type through `@ScaledMetric`. The dots run on the clock rather than a repeating animation so they stay in phase however long the pill is up; VoiceOver hears the label with "Thinking" as its value and skips the dots. Reduce Transparency swaps the material for an opaque secondary background.
- Reduce Motion pauses the wave on a still frame and holds the dots.

### Parameters

- `size`: Diameter of the ball in points. 18–30 inside a pill, 64 at avatar size.
- `palette`: The kind of work the colour portrays: `.siri` (thinking, default), `.searching`, `.reading` or `.writing`, or your own `Palette(bands:ground:crest:rimCool:rimWarm:)`. A change crossfades over 0.8s; the motion never changes.

## Silk (`Silk`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/backgrounds/silk
Category: Backgrounds. iOS 17.0+. Metal shader.
Files: Silk.swift, Silk.metal
Install: npx swiftpieces add Silk

A slowly folding silk surface lit by a movable light and shaded from a real gradient normal in a Metal shader, in house block fabrics and an adaptive standard style, with optional device-tilt lighting.

Flowing silk background. Copy `Silk.metal` alongside this file. The shader samples the fold height field three times to build a normal, then shades it with Blinn-Phong so the sheen sits on the folds facing the light.

### Notes

- Requires `Silk.metal` in the same target. The shader samples the fold height field three times per pixel (centre, +x, +y) to build a real gradient normal, then shades it with Blinn-Phong, so the sheen lands on the folds facing `light` instead of being painted by height.
- `light` is a `UnitPoint` in the view's coordinates; move it to change where the highlight sits. `Style.depth` is the fold contrast and `Style.shine` the highlight tightness.
- `tiltLight` starts a private `CMMotionManager` source at 30 Hz, relative to the attitude at start, low-passed. It stops on disappear and whenever `scenePhase` leaves `.active`, and is a no-op in the simulator.
- Reduce Motion freezes the fold animation; with `tiltLight` the light still follows the device, which is user-driven, not decorative.
- `Style.standard` (default) is stone with a white sheen in light and charcoal with a sand sheen in dark. `.tangerine`, `.sky`, `.butter`, `.sage`, `.lilac` and `.sand` are solid house-block fabrics for panels and cards; put `#141414` ink on them. `.ink`, `.graphite`, `.paper` and `.indigo` still work.
- The radial fold term is centred off-screen, so no pinch point appears in the middle of the view.
- The `#Preview` is the standard fabric alone, full bleed, with nothing on top of it.

### Parameters

- `style`: Fabric color, sheen color, fold contrast and highlight tightness. `.standard` (default) follows light and dark; `.tangerine`, `.sky`, `.butter`, `.sage`, `.lilac` and `.sand` are solid house-block fabrics for panels and cards. `.ink`, `.graphite`, `.paper` and `.indigo` remain available.
- `light`: Where the light comes from, in unit coordinates of the view. Top-left by default.
- `tiltLight`: When true, the device's attitude moves the light. Uses Core Motion and stops whenever the scene is not active.
- `scale`: Pattern zoom; larger is finer folds.
- `speed`: Time multiplier.

## Touch Grid (`TouchGrid`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/backgrounds/touch-grid
Category: Backgrounds. iOS 17.0+.
Files: TouchGrid.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add TouchGrid

A Canvas dot grid that swells and warms into a house block color under the finger, springs back on release, and sends one dissipating ripple out from a tap.

Interactive dot grid. Resting dots are a tonal ramp on `Style.dot` (`.primary` by default, so both color schemes work); under the finger they swell and take on `Style.highlight`, a solid house block.

### Notes

- Everything is drawn in one `Canvas` inside a `TimelineView` that pauses when nothing is pressed, springing or rippling, so an idle grid costs nothing. A short task clears expired springs and ripples so the timeline can pause again.
- Release is a damped spring computed per frame (`e^-7t · cos 10t`), so the dots overshoot slightly below their resting size before settling. While dragging the field follows the finger directly.
- A tap (moved under 8 pt, held under 0.3 s) emits one ripple ring that eases outward and widens as it fades; ripples are capped at three. Reduce Motion disables only the ripple; the highlight and spring remain.
- The highlight is a tonal ramp on `.primary` (`baseOpacity` up to 0.92) with a 3.2x swell, so it matches any tint and both color schemes.
- The `.selection` haptic fires at most every 60 ms and only when the finger crosses into a new grid cell.
- `probe` drives the grid without a finger, for previews, hints, or onboarding.
- `style:` sets the resting dot color (`.primary` by default) and the block the dots take on as they lift. `.standard` warms into tangerine; `.sky`, `.lilac`, `.sage` and `.butter` use the other blocks, and `.mono` keeps the single-tone ramp.
- The `#Preview` is the grid alone on the house ground, full bleed; touch it to swell, release to spring back, tap for a ripple.

### Parameters

- `spacing`: Distance between dots.
- `dotSize`: Resting dot diameter.
- `radius`: Influence radius of the touch.
- `baseOpacity`: Opacity of resting dots on `.primary`.
- `ripples`: Whether a tap emits a ripple ring. Reduce Motion disables ripples regardless.
- `probe`: Optional programmatic touch point for previews and onboarding hints. Setting it back to `nil` triggers the release spring; a probe held under 0.3 s emits a ripple like a tap.
- `style`: Resting dot color and the block color dots take on under the finger. `.standard` (default) warms into tangerine; `.sky`, `.lilac`, `.sage` and `.butter` use the other blocks; `.mono` keeps the original single-tone ramp.

## Flip Card (`FlipCard`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/cards/flip-card
Category: Cards. iOS 17.0+.
Files: FlipCard.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add FlipCard

A two-sided card you flip by tap or by dragging sideways. The drag scrubs the rotation, release commits or snaps back by velocity, the card lifts toward you mid-turn with a layered shadow that slides off the raised edge, and each face shades as it turns edge-on.

Two-sided card with tap-to-flip and drag-to-flip.

### Notes

- One `DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)` handles everything: touch-down tilts the card toward the finger and scales it to 0.98, an 8pt sideways move turns into a scrub where the full card width equals 180°, and a lift without movement is a tap.
- Release commits when `predictedEndTranslation` projects past 90° in either direction, so a flick finishes the flip and a slow drag that stops short snaps back. Dragging past a full turn rubber-bands at 200°.
- Each face darkens with `brightness` as it turns edge-on and hides past 90°; the back is pre-rotated by -180° so it lands unmirrored. The shadow slides opposite the lifted edge and widens mid-flip.
- The angle accumulates (0, 180, 360...) so repeated flips keep rotating the same way; `isFlipped:` stays in sync in both directions.
- A soft impact fires as the visible face changes. Reduce Motion replaces the rotation with a crossfade that the drag still scrubs.
- **v2:** the card lifts 6% toward you at the edge-on point, sits on a layered shadow (a tight contact shadow plus a soft key shadow that slides off the raised edge), a soft-light band crosses each face as it turns, and the scrub rubber-bands past a half turn. Touch-down gives a light impact.
- `style:` (`FlipCard.Style`) tunes `cornerRadius`, `shadow`/`shadowOpacity` (tripled in dark mode), `lift`, `pressScale`, `pressTilt`, and `shading`. `onFlip:` reports each committed flip. A disabled card dims and ignores touches.
- The example is a vocabulary flashcard: a butter front with a heavy word and a sky back with the meaning. The preview shows the card alone, with no surrounding UI.
- For a full card screen with number masking and controls, see the Pro Card Details screen (`payment-card`).

### Parameters

- `isFlipped`: Optional binding to drive the flip externally. Leave nil to let the card manage its own state; taps and drags still update the binding when one is passed.
- `style`: Depth, lift, press, and shading tuning. `.standard` uses the house values; the faces bring their own color.
- `onFlip`: Called after a flip commits, with `true` when the back is now showing.
- `front`: Front face. Give it its own shape and surface; the card only rotates, lifts, shades, and shadows it.
- `back`: Back face, shown after the flip. It is pre-rotated so text is never mirrored.

## Motion Card (`MotionCard`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/cards/motion-card
Category: Cards. iOS 17.0+.
Files: MotionCard.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add MotionCard

A solid color card that tilts with the device's attitude through an exponential filter, with a fixed-light sheen and a layered shadow that slide as it turns. Press settles it flat and scales it down with a light impact, and Core Motion stops whenever the scene is not active.

Attitude-driven card with a fixed-light sheen, tracking shadow, and press feedback.

### Notes

- Core Motion roll and pitch are measured relative to the pose at the moment updates start, so the card sits flat however the phone is held, then run through an exponential filter (15% per sample at 60Hz) that removes hand jitter without perceptible lag.
- Motion starts on appear and whenever `scenePhase` becomes `.active`, and stops on disappear and in any other phase, so the sensors never run in the background. In the simulator, and with Reduce Motion, the card is static with a fixed light.
- Pass `attitude:` (-1...1 per axis) to drive the tilt yourself for previews, tests, or the simulator; it replaces device motion entirely.
- The specular highlight is an 11% white radial gradient whose center moves opposite the tilt, as a reflection of a fixed light would; the shadow slides the same way and widens with the tilt magnitude.
- The card draws its own surface (`secondarySystemGroupedBackground`, 0.5pt hairline, continuous corners) under your content. Press scales to 0.98 with a light impact; a lift within 10pt runs `action` if one is set.
- The motion source is a nested `@Observable` class marked `fileprivate`, because the macro's generated extension cannot see a `private` nested type.
- **v2:** the card draws a solid block (`style.fill`, tangerine by default) with dark ink, a soft-light sheen plus a faint far-side shade that follow a fixed light, and a two-layer shadow. Pressing settles the tilt halfway to flat, tightens the shadow, and scales to `pressScale`. Disabled cards desaturate.
- `style:` (`MotionCard.Style`) sets `fill`, `foreground`, `sheen`, `shadowOpacity`, and `pressScale`; `cornerRadius` now defaults to 26.
- The example is a film ticket with light seat numerals and perforation notches.
- For a full card screen, see the Pro Card Details screen (`payment-card`).

### Parameters

- `maxAngle`: Maximum tilt in degrees on each axis.
- `cornerRadius`: Corner radius of the card surface (continuous).
- `attitude`: Optional fixed tilt, -1...1 on each axis, that replaces device motion. Useful for previews, tests, and the simulator.
- `style`: The card's fill, ink, sheen, shadow, and press. `.standard` is a tangerine block with dark ink.
- `action`: Optional tap handler. The card always scales on press; this runs on a clean tap.
- `content`: Card content, laid over the card's own surface. It inherits `style.foreground`.

## Parallax Card (`ParallaxCard`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/cards/parallax-card
Category: Cards. iOS 17.0+.
Files: ParallaxCard.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add ParallaxCard

An image card whose picture drifts slower than the scroll while a solid caption block drifts slower still, so the card reads in layers. Press lifts it with a deeper shadow and nudges the trailing glyph, and the caption is composed from eyebrow, title, metadata, and trailing glyph slots.

Image card with two-layer scroll parallax, press-to-lift, and a slotted caption.

### Notes

- The drift is computed with `visualEffect` from `proxy.frame(in: .scrollView)`, so the card works inside any `ScrollView` or `List` without a named coordinate space. Outside a scroll view it renders static.
- Three layers move at different rates: the image at `parallax`, the caption at a third of that, and the scrim scales from 1.3x tall at the viewport center to 0.9x at the edges, so the bottom reads tighter as the card leaves.
- The image is oversized by `height * parallax` on each side and clipped, so no background shows at the extremes.
- Pass `action:` to make the card a `Button`; the press style scales it to 1.02 and deepens the shadow with a fast press-in and a springy release. Without an action it keeps a resting shadow.
- The caption is slots: `eyebrow` (uppercased, tracked), `title`, `metadata` (dot-separated row), and `trailingSymbol` (in a translucent circle). All text is white over the scrim, which is fine on light photos in both color schemes.
- Reduce Motion disables the drift and the scrim scaling; the composition is unchanged.
- **v2:** the caption defaults to a solid inset block (`.block`) that drifts at a third of the picture's rate, with a heavy title, a dimmed metadata row, and the trailing glyph in an ink circle that nudges toward its arrow on press. `ParallaxCard.Style.scrim` restores white text over the tightening scrim.
- `style:` (`ParallaxCard.Style`) sets `caption`, `captionFill`, `captionInk`, and `shadowOpacity`; `cornerRadius` now defaults to 26. The press state reaches the caption through the environment, so VoiceOver still reads the button label.
- The example renders each picture as a flat composition (a color ground, a disc, a cropped giant word) with `ImageRenderer`; no photos ship with the piece.
- For an expanding card on a full discover screen, see the Pro Discover screen (`hero-expand`).

### Parameters

- `image`: The picture to show, scaled to fill.
- `eyebrow`: Optional small uppercase line above the title, for a category or date.
- `title`: Title drawn in the caption.
- `metadata`: Optional short facts shown in a dot-separated row under the title.
- `trailingSymbol`: Optional SF Symbol drawn in a circle at the caption's trailing end, for example "arrow.up.right".
- `height`: Card height.
- `parallax`: How far the image drifts, as a fraction of `height` on each side. The caption drifts at a third of that. 0 disables the effect.
- `cornerRadius`: Corner radius of the card.
- `style`: Caption treatment and colors. `.standard` is a butter caption block with dark ink; `.scrim` puts white text over a darkened bottom edge.
- `action`: Optional tap handler. When set, the card lifts on press and reads as a button.

## Swipe Deck (`SwipeDeck`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/cards/swipe-deck
Category: Cards. iOS 17.0+.
Files: SwipeDeck.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add SwipeDeck

A gesture-driven card stack: the top card follows the finger and swings from its base, a solid outcome badge fades in for the direction you are heading and locks at the threshold, the cards beneath rise as it leaves, and release past the threshold or a flick throws it left, right, or up.

Swipeable card stack over Identifiable data. The deck removes the top item from `items` after each throw.

### Notes

- The deck is the source of truth for nothing: it removes the top item from the bound `items` array after each throw and reports the direction through `onSwipe`. Append items to keep the stack going, or watch the array run empty.
- Directions use SwiftUI's `Edge` so the file stays self-contained: `.trailing` (swiped right), `.leading` (left), `.top` (up). Down is never committed; a downward drag springs back.
- Commit is decided from `predictedEndTranslation`, so a flick throws even from a short drag. The horizontal threshold is 40% of the width, the upward one 30% of the height. A `.selection` tick fires the moment the drag crosses either, and a solid impact fires on the throw.
- The card flies along its actual vector (drag plus velocity) for 1.6x the deck's larger dimension, then is removed without a transition while the next card springs up from 0.95 scale and 14pt lower.
- Rotation is 14° per card width with a bottom anchor, so the card swings like it is pinned at the base. Reduce Motion drops the rotation and fades the card out in place instead of throwing it.
- `swipe:` is a command binding: set it to a direction to throw programmatically (from buttons, a keyboard shortcut, or a preview loop); the deck resets it to nil. VoiceOver gets "Swipe right", "Swipe left", and "Swipe up" actions on the top card.
- Give the deck an explicit frame; cards are sized to fill it.
- **v2:** outcome badges. While the top card heads left, right, or up, a solid badge (Skip, Keep, Save by default) fades and scales in for that direction and locks with a pop at the threshold. Cards further down sit in shade and brighten as they rise, and the top card's shadow deepens with the drag.
- `style:` (`SwipeDeck.Style`) sets the three `SwipeDeck.Badge` values (title, symbol, fill, ink; nil hides one), `cornerRadius`, `shadowOpacity`, and `emptyMessage`, a dashed slot drawn when the deck runs out. `.plain` turns badges and the slot off. VoiceOver actions use the badge titles.

### Parameters

- `items`: Bound array of cards, top first. Swiped items are removed from the front.
- `swipe`: Optional command binding. Set it to `.leading`, `.trailing`, or `.top` to throw the top card programmatically; the deck resets it to nil.
- `visibleCount`: How many cards are drawn in the stack.
- `style`: Outcome badges, stack depth, and the empty slot. `.standard` shows Skip, Keep, and Save badges in house blocks.
- `onSwipe`: Called after a card is thrown, with the direction (`.leading`, `.trailing`, or `.top`) and the item.
- `onTap`: Optional tap handler for the top card.
- `card`: Builds one card. Give it its own shape and surface; the deck sizes it to fill the deck's frame.

## Commit Button (`CommitButton`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/controls/commit-button
Category: Controls. iOS 17.0+.
Files: CommitButton.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add CommitButton

An async action button driven by one idle/loading/success/error/disabled phase: a signal capsule collapses to a spinning ring, closes it and blooms into a sage success block with a drawn check, or re-expands as a butter error block that shakes and doubles as retry.

Async action button whose whole lifecycle is one bound `phase`.

### Notes

- `phase` is a `Binding` so the button can return itself to `.idle` after the success hold (`successHold`, default 900ms); everything else is set by you: `.loading` in the action, `.success` or `.error("message")` when the work finishes.
- States, all from `Style.standard`: idle is a signal capsule with dark ink; pressed squashes and darkens; loading collapses to a circle with an ink arc; success closes the arc, turns sage and draws the check, then, if you pass `successTitle` ("Saved"), blooms back into a sage capsule with an ink check disc; error re-expands as a butter block with an ink "!" disc, rolls the label to the message and shakes; disabled uses the raised color with muted ink.
- Tapping in the error state fires the action again, so the message doubles as a retry (VoiceOver hears "Double tap to try again"). The button ignores taps while loading or succeeding without dimming.
- `tint` and `errorTint` still work: they override the style fills and switch that state's ink to white. For full control pass a `Style` with your own fills, ink, height and font.
- Reduce Motion crossfades the label, shortens the collapse and skips the shake offset; the haptics stay.
- Need a slide-to-act confirmation with an amount and recipient? Swift Pieces Pro has the Send Money screen (`swipe-to-confirm`).

### Parameters

- `title`: Idle label.
- `phase`: Bound `.idle`, `.loading`, `.success`, `.error(message)` or `.disabled`. The button returns itself to `.idle` after a success hold.
- `tint`: Overrides the style's fill while idle and loading, with white ink. `nil` uses `style.fill`.
- `errorTint`: Overrides the style's error fill, with white ink. `nil` uses `style.errorFill`.
- `successHold`: How long the success state stays before the label expands back.
- `successTitle`: Text shown beside the check on success, such as "Saved". `nil` keeps the success state a closed circle.
- `style`: Fills, ink, height and type. `.standard` is the house palette: signal, sage for success, butter for errors.
- `action`: Tap handler. Set `phase` to `.loading` inside it and to `.success` or `.error` when the work finishes.

## Elastic Button (`ElasticButton`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/controls/elastic-button
Category: Controls. iOS 17.0+.
Files: ElasticButton.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add ElasticButton

A ButtonStyle that squashes toward the touch point, stretches with rubber-band resistance when dragged, deepens after a hold and snaps back with a spring. Optional solid surfaces (signal, block, raised) press into their own soft shadow and darken under the finger.

Squash-and-stretch press for any `Button`. Apply with `.buttonStyle(.elastic)`, or `.buttonStyle(.elastic(.signal))` to also draw the surface.

### Notes

- It is a `ButtonStyle`, so it works on any `Button`: `.buttonStyle(.elastic)` adds only the motion, `.buttonStyle(.elastic(.signal))` also draws the surface, and `.elastic(squash:bounce:haptics:style:)` tunes both.
- `Style` presets come from the house palette: `.standard` (motion only, your label keeps its look), `.signal` for the one primary action, `.block(.lilac)` and the other blocks for secondary actions with dark ink, `.raised` for quiet ones. `radius`, `height` (never below 44) and `padding` are adjustable.
- States: at rest a drawn surface sits on a soft two-layer shadow; pressed it squashes toward the finger, darkens and the shadow flattens; after a 350ms hold it presses 0.03 deeper and darkens further with a soft impact; a drag past 44pt cancels the press with a soft impact; disabled surfaces switch to the raised color with muted ink instead of fading.
- The touch point comes from a simultaneous zero-distance drag, so the squash leans 60% of the way toward the finger, the shape stretches along the drag axis with rubber-band resistance, and the offset follows at 35%. Release uses `.snappy` plus `bounce` as extra bounce.
- Reduce Motion keeps the scale and darken but removes the lean, stretch and offset. Disabled buttons play no haptics.

### Parameters

- `squash`: Scale while pressed, anchored toward the touch point. Holding 350ms eases 0.03 deeper.
- `bounce`: Extra bounce added to the `.snappy` release spring.
- `haptics`: Plays a solid impact on press, a soft one when the hold deepens, and a soft one when a drag cancels.
- `style`: The surface drawn behind the label. `.standard` draws nothing and only adds the motion; `.signal`, `.raised` and `.block(_:)` draw a solid capsule with ink, layered depth that compresses on press, and a darken under the finger.

## Fan Stack (`FanStack`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/controls/fan-stack
Category: Controls. iOS 17.0+.
Files: FanStack.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add FanStack

Overlapping block-color avatars that fan apart on tap or hold with staggered springs, dissolve the +N pill into the hidden faces, and let a drag scrub across them: the avatar under the finger lifts, shows a name tag and ticks a haptic, and releasing selects it.

Avatar group that expands into a selectable fan.

### Notes

- Tap toggles the fan; a 300ms hold fans it and keeps the touch live so you can scrub. While fanned, the avatar under the finger lifts (scale 1.18, a 4pt rise, soft shadow), shows its full name in an inverted tag above, bolds its first name below, and ticks `.selection` per crossing. Releasing on it calls `onSelect` and collapses; releasing a hold on empty space leaves the fan open; a tap on empty space closes it.
- Initials sit on solid house blocks with dark ink, picked by a stable FNV-1a hash of the name. `Style` sets the block list, ink, the cut-out `ring` (match it to the surface behind the stack), the "+N" pill and the name tag.
- Every name is in the hierarchy at all times. Collapsed, avatars past `max` sit hidden at the "+N" pill's position, so on expand they emerge from where the pill dissolves. Springs stagger 35ms per avatar, reversed on collapse.
- The tag draws 34pt above the avatars and first names 24pt below while fanned (the frame grows for the names only), so leave room above the stack.
- `images` is a parallel array; it may be shorter than `names`, and `nil` entries fall back to initials.
- Reduce Motion removes the stagger and the lift; the hovered avatar shows a ring instead. VoiceOver reads the collapsed stack as one element ("Priya Raman, Jonas Weber, and 3 more", double tap to expand) and each avatar as its own button once fanned.

### Parameters

- `names`: Full names, in display order. First name is drawn on top while collapsed.
- `images`: Optional parallel array of images; `nil` entries fall back to initials on a block color.
- `size`: Diameter of each avatar in points.
- `max`: Avatars shown while collapsed before the rest fold into "+N". All fan open.
- `overlap`: Fraction of `size` each avatar overlaps the previous one while collapsed, 0–1.
- `onSelect`: Called with the name released on while fanned. Also used by VoiceOver's per-avatar action.
- `isFanned`: Optional binding to fan or collapse programmatically; written back when the user toggles it.
- `style`: Block colors, ink, the cut-out ring and the name tag. `.standard` is the house palette; set `ring` to the color behind the stack.

## Hold To Confirm (`HoldToConfirm`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/controls/hold-to-confirm
Category: Controls. iOS 17.0+.
Files: HoldToConfirm.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add HoldToConfirm

A press-and-hold capsule for destructive or important actions: a solid fill sweeps from the leading puck while held, passes three milestone dots with rising haptics, inverts the label under it, rewinds with a spring on early release and settles into a sage confirmed block.

Hold to confirm. The label inverts as the fill passes under it; letting go or dragging off rewinds.

### Notes

- The track is a raised capsule with an ink puck holding the symbol. While held, a solid fill sweeps from under the puck across the track, driven by a `TimelineView`; an ink copy of the label and puck is masked to the fill, so both invert as it passes.
- Three milestone dots sit at 25, 50 and 75%. Each pops as the fill passes it, in step with a soft impact of rising intensity; `.success` and the action fire at 100%. Releasing early or dragging more than 16pt off the capsule cancels and the fill rewinds with a spring.
- On commit the fill turns `committedFill` (sage), the puck symbol replaces itself with a check, and the label rolls to `committedTitle` if you pass one ("Deleted"). It returns to idle after 1.4s.
- `Style.standard` sweeps signal for destructive actions; `Style.butter` is a calmer confirm. `tint` still works and overrides the fill with white ink. Disabled (`.disabled(true)`) desaturates the control and blocks the gesture.
- Phases: `idle`, `holding`, `committed`, `cancelled`, `disabled`. VoiceOver reads a button with the hint "Touch and hold to confirm"; its activate action performs the action directly.
- Reduce Motion halves `duration`, drops the press scale and the dot pop, and crossfades the label; the fill still sweeps.
- Want slide to act instead of hold? Swift Pieces Pro has the Send Money screen (`swipe-to-confirm`).

### Parameters

- `title`: Label while idle and holding.
- `systemImage`: Optional SF Symbol drawn in the leading puck.
- `duration`: Seconds the hold must last. Halved under Reduce Motion.
- `tint`: Overrides the style's fill (and tints the track) with white ink on the fill. `nil` uses `style`.
- `phase`: Optional binding that mirrors `idle`, `holding`, `committed` and `cancelled`; set it to `.holding` to start a sweep programmatically, `.idle` to cancel one.
- `committedTitle`: Text beside the check once the hold completes, such as "Deleted". `nil` shows the check alone.
- `style`: Track, fill, ink and committed colors plus height. `.standard` is the house palette with a signal fill.
- `action`: Called once when the hold completes. VoiceOver's activate action calls it directly.

## Timer Dial (`TimerDial`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/controls/timer-dial
Category: Controls. iOS 17.0+.
Files: TimerDial.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add TimerDial

A countdown ring you set by dragging its knob around like the Timer dial, with a tick per step and a heavier detent every 5s. A solid block ring over a minute-tick scale, light display numerals, a breathing signal warning zone, a sage finish, and a determinate progress mode.

Settable countdown ring, or a determinate progress ring with the same look.

### Notes

- While idle or paused, dragging around the ring sets `seconds` like the Timer dial: the angle maps to `0...maxSeconds` in `step` increments, with `.selection` per step and a rigid impact on every multiple of 5. The value clamps at both ends instead of wrapping. The knob grows while the dial can be set. VoiceOver adjusts it with swipe up/down.
- The look comes from `Style.standard`: a solid tangerine ring over a raised track, an ink knob with a soft shadow, a 60-tick scale inside that brightens under the value, and light display numerals reading `m:ss` with the leading `0:` dimmed. `Style.sky` swaps the ring; `colors` still overrides it (several colors draw an angular gradient).
- Timing is anchored to a start date and rendered by `TimelineView`, so the ring never drifts; a single `.task` sleeps until the finish. Toggling `isRunning` off banks the elapsed time; on resumes. After finishing, `true` restarts from `seconds`. Changing `seconds` resets.
- At or below `warningAt` the signal ring fades in over the base ring, the digits turn signal, the dial breathes ±1.2% once per second with a soft impact per second. Finishing springs a full sage ring in, hides the knob and plays `.success`.
- `TimerDial(progress:)` is the determinate mode: the same ring and knob with a percent readout (dimmed %) and no clock or dial. Turn `showsTicks` off and lower `digitSize` for small rings.
- Digits scale with Dynamic Type relative to `.largeTitle` and never outgrow the ring. Reduce Motion drops the breathing, the per-second haptic, the numeric roll and the finish spring, and ticks the ring once per second.
- Need a whole focus session with task binding and breaks? Swift Pieces Pro has the Focus screen (`focus-timer`).

### Parameters

- `seconds`: Bound countdown length. Dragging around the ring while idle or paused rewrites it.
- `isRunning`: Set `true` to run, `false` to pause. Flips to `false` when the countdown finishes; set it back to `true` to restart.
- `step`: Seconds per dial detent. Every multiple of 5 plays a heavier tick.
- `maxSeconds`: Value at a full turn of the dial.
- `warningAt`: Remaining seconds at or below which the ring turns to `style.warning` and breathes.
- `lineWidth`: Ring thickness in points.
- `colors`: Overrides `style.fill`: one color for a flat ring, or several for an angular gradient. `nil` uses the style.
- `caption`: Text under the digits. Defaults to the phase (Ready, Remaining, Paused, Done).
- `style`: Ring, track, knob, tick, warning and finish colors plus the numeral size. `.standard` is the house palette with a tangerine ring.
- `onFinish`: Called once when the ring reaches zero.
- `progress`: Determinate mode: a 0–1 value with a percent readout and no clock.

## Live Stat (`LiveStat`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/data/live-stat
Category: Data. iOS 17.0+.
Files: LiveStat.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add LiveStat

A metric tile with a light display-scale value that rolls with a spring and dims its decimals, a solid delta block, a sparkline you hold and scrub to retarget the value live, a press that expands the line into a taller chart with low and high, and a solid color block variant.

KPI tile with a rolling value, delta chip, and a scrubbable sparkline that expands on press.

### Notes

- The value is an `Animatable` text in light 40 pt display type with dimmed decimals. A spring interpolates real numbers through your `format`, and in-flight frames round to the target's own decimal places, so whole-number formats never flash a long fraction mid-roll.
- Touch and hold the tile for 280 ms to scrub: a rule and a dot ride the sparkline, the value retargets to each point with a short spring, and `.selection` ticks per point. Release rolls back to the live value. At rest the dot marks the latest value.
- A plain tap expands the tile into a 120 pt chart drawn by the same `Shape`, adding a dashed baseline at the first value and a low and high row. Moving more than 10 pt before the hold completes cancels both, so the tile can live in a scrolling grid. States: resting, pressed (97% with a flatter shadow), scrubbing, expanded.
- The delta is a solid block with ink: sage for up, tangerine for down. Under Increase Contrast it gains a 1 pt outline.
- `Style`: `.standard` is a white or charcoal tile; `.block(_:)` fills the tile with a color block and turns the value, line, and dot to ink, with the delta as an ink pill. `tint` overrides the sparkline color.
- Reduce Motion skips the press scale, the count-up, and the draw-on. VoiceOver reads label and value, double-tap expands, and swipe up or down scrubs history.
- A full dashboard screen ships in Swift Pieces Pro (`dashboard-screen`).

### Parameters

- `label`: Metric name shown above the value.
- `value`: Current value. Changing it rolls the number from the previous one.
- `format`: Number format for the value, for example `.number` or `.currency(code: "USD")`. Defaults to `.number`.
- `delta`: Optional fractional change (0.12 is +12%) shown as a solid chip: sage for up, tangerine for down.
- `series`: History drawn as the sparkline, oldest first. Hold and drag it to scrub.
- `tint`: Sparkline color. Defaults to the style's `line`.
- `expanded`: Optional binding to the expanded state, for driving it from outside.
- `style`: Tile, text, and chip colors. Defaults to `.standard`, a surface tile; `.block(_:)` fills the tile with a color block and dark ink.

## Odometer (`Odometer`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/data/odometer
Category: Data. iOS 17.0+.
Files: Odometer.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add Odometer

A number whose digits roll on individual slots like a mechanical counter, carrying from the low digits up so unchanged digits never move, with softened slot edges while rolling, dimmed decimals, a separate sign, a solid delta block, and a dashed loading state.

Slot-machine number with a single spring-driven `Animatable` value behind every digit.

### Notes

- One `Animatable` number drives every slot. Each digit's roll is derived from that number and carries upward only while the digit below passes 9, so higher digits stay perfectly still until a carry reaches them. While a digit is between faces its slot edges soften, like a drum turning behind a window. The roll runs on `.smooth` with a duration that grows gently with the size of the change; there is no per-frame loop.
- The layout (grouping separators, decimal separator, currency symbol) is read from the formatted target once per change. Use plain decimal or currency styles; compact notation such as `1.2K` will not match the rolled digits. Leading symbols always show, and the number never gives up width to the delta pill.
- Decimals and their separator are dimmed by default. The sign is its own glyph and slides in or out at the zero crossing. After each change a solid delta block shows the signed amount for 1.6 s: sage for up, tangerine for down, ink text.
- `Style` sets `up`, `down`, `ink`, `muted`, `dimsFraction`, and `tintsWhileRolling` (tints the digits until the roll settles; best on dark grounds).
- `isLoading` swaps every digit for a dash; the first real value rolls up from zero. Reduce Motion replaces the roll with a short ease.
- VoiceOver reads the final formatted value only, never the intermediate frames. Apply `.font` to the `Odometer` (light weights suit it); slot sizes are measured from that font.
- A full dashboard screen ships in Swift Pieces Pro (`dashboard-screen`).

### Parameters

- `value`: The target value. Changing it rolls the digits from the current value.
- `format`: A decimal `FormatStyle` from `Double` to `String`, for example `.number.precision(.fractionLength(0))` or `.currency(code: "USD")`. Defaults to whole numbers.
- `isLoading`: Shows a dash in every digit slot instead of a value; the first real value rolls up from zero.
- `showsDelta`: Shows a signed delta pill next to the number for a moment after each change.
- `ticksOnSettle`: Plays a `.selection` haptic when a roll finishes.
- `style`: Delta block colors, decimal dimming, and roll tinting. Defaults to `.standard`: sage for up, tangerine for down, dimmed decimals, no tint while rolling.

## Ring Breakdown (`RingBreakdown`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/data/ring-breakdown
Category: Data. iOS 17.0+.
Files: RingBreakdown.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add RingBreakdown

A composition ring of solid color blocks with rounded seams that you scrub by dragging around it, with a haptic at each slice boundary, a radial lift for the selected slice while the rest step back to the surface, a light display-scale center figure, and legend rows that turn into the slice's block.

Ring chart with scrub-to-select, a lifted slice, and a built-in legend.

### Notes

- Slices are solid color blocks from the house palette (tangerine, sky, butter, sage, lilac, sand), separated by a 4 pt gap with rounded ends. Each slice is filled and stroked with a round join, so the corners stay soft at any size.
- Drag anywhere on the ring and the selection follows your finger around it, with a `.selection` tick at every slice boundary. Release keeps the selection; tap the hole or the selected legend row to clear it.
- The selected slice lifts 6 pt outward along its mid-angle with a soft shadow while the others step back to a solid resting color, never a faded wash. The center shows an uppercase label, a light figure with dimmed decimals, and the share as a pill in the slice's color. The legend row turns into the slice's block with ink text.
- `tint` overrides the first slice; `color` on a slice overrides any slice. `Style` sets `blocks`, `rest`, `ink`, `text`, `muted`, `gap`, and `cornerRadius`. The default thickness is 34 pt.
- The ring is one VoiceOver element: it reads the selected slice or the total, and swiping up or down moves the selection. Legend rows are 48 pt buttons with their value. Reduce Motion drops the lift and the sweep-in but keeps the state change.

- A full budget screen built on a spending ring ships in Swift Pieces Pro (`spending-ring`).

### Parameters

- `slices`: Parts of the whole, drawn clockwise from the top. Labels must be unique.
- `thickness`: Ring thickness in points.
- `tint`: Color of the first slice. Defaults to the style's first block; later slices take the next blocks unless a slice sets `color`.
- `format`: Number format for the center value and legend, for example `.number` or `.currency(code: "USD")`. Defaults to `.number`.
- `showsLegend`: Show the tappable legend rows below the ring.
- `selection`: Optional binding to the selected slice id, for driving selection from outside.
- `style`: Slice blocks, ink, and surface colors. Defaults to `.standard`: tangerine, sky, butter, sage, lilac, and sand.

## Scrub Chart (`ScrubChart`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/data/scrub-chart
Category: Data. iOS 17.0+.
Files: ScrubChart.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add ScrubChart

A line or bar chart component with a light display-scale readout and dimmed decimals, a solid delta block, a flag that rides the scrub rule, hold-and-drag range selection with delta and percent, and a block range picker that morphs the line between datasets.

Time-series chart with scrubbing, range selection, and a morphing range picker.

### Notes

- The readout is display type: an uppercase meta line (range, point time, or held span), a light 44 pt figure with its decimals dimmed, and a solid delta block beside it: sage for up, tangerine for down, ink text.
- One finger drags to scrub: a rule and a butter dot ride the line, a flag at the top of the rule shows the point's time, and `.selection` ticks at each data point. Holding still for 300 ms before moving pins that point as an anchor and the drag becomes a range: a solid band fills the span and the figure shows the signed change with its percent.
- Every series is normalized to 0...1 for drawing, so the y-scale never jumps between ranges. In `.line` mode datasets are resampled to 64 positions and switching ranges morphs the line; in `.bars` mode bars animate to their new heights and the active bar takes the accent block. Under Reduce Motion the switch is a short crossfade.
- At rest: no y-axis, one dashed baseline at the first value, monospaced min and max markers, the latest point as a butter dot, and three uppercase date labels whose format follows the span of the range. The picker is a butter block on a solid track, 44 pt tall.

An empty series shows "No data yet".
- VoiceOver gets one element with the latest value and change; swipe up or down steps the scrub point.
- A full dashboard screen ships in Swift Pieces Pro (`dashboard-screen`).

### Parameters

- `series`: One dataset per range button, in display order. A single entry hides the picker.
- `mode`: `.line` draws a smoothed line with min and max markers; `.bars` draws one bar per point.
- `tint`: Line and bar color. Defaults to the style's `line`, the house text color.
- `format`: Number format for readouts, for example `.number` or `.currency(code: "USD")`. Defaults to `.number`.
- `range`: Optional binding to the selected series index, for driving the picker from outside.
- `style`: Accent, delta, band, and numeral settings. Defaults to `.standard`: a butter accent, sage for up, tangerine for down.

## Outcome Screen (`OutcomeScreen`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/feedback/outcome-screen
Category: Feedback. iOS 17.0+.
Files: OutcomeScreen.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add OutcomeScreen

A success, failure or empty outcome view sharing one choreography, where a ring draws, floods into a solid color block, the mark strokes in dark ink, one pulse lands with a haptic, and a heavy headline and a single signal action rise, with async retry and a details block for failures.

Success, failure or empty outcome view with one shared choreography: a ring, a solid block, an ink mark and one signal action.

### Notes

- Three outcomes share one choreography, run once per appearance: a ring draws in ink, a solid block floods out of it (sage for `.success`, butter for `.failure`, sky for `.empty`), the mark strokes in dark ink via `trim`, one pulse and the haptic land together, then the copy and actions rise. Change the view's `.id` to replay it.
- `.empty` draws an open tray and plays a light impact, for first-run and no-results states.
- The headline is set heavy and tight at `.largeTitle`; `eyebrow` adds a small uppercase line above it. The primary action is the one `signal` capsule; `secondary` is a quiet text button.
- `Style` holds the three blocks, the ink, the signal colors, text colors and the details surface, with house palette defaults that adapt to light and dark. `accent` still overrides the block.
- On failure, `retry` turns the primary button into "Try again" with a spinner while the async work runs; `details` adds a rounded block that expands to selectable monospaced text.
- Under Reduce Motion everything appears at once and the pulse is skipped; haptics still fire.
- For a complete purchase screen, see the Pro Purchase screen.

### Parameters

- `outcome`: `.success`, `.failure` or `.empty`. Sets the block, mark, and haptic.
- `title`: Headline, set heavy and tight.
- `message`: Supporting copy.
- `primaryTitle`: Primary button title when `retry` is not used.
- `primaryAction`: Primary button handler when `retry` is not used.
- `retry`: Optional async handler for failures; the primary button becomes "Try again" and shows a spinner until it returns.
- `secondary`: Optional quiet second action.
- `details`: Optional technical text behind a "Details" disclosure on failures.
- `accent`: Overrides the block color behind the mark. Defaults to the outcome's color in `style`.
- `eyebrow`: Optional small uppercase line above the title, such as "Synced 10:42".
- `style`: Block, signal and text colors. `.standard` is sage for success, butter for failure and sky for empty, with a signal primary button.

## Rating Scrub (`RatingScrub`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/feedback/rating-scrub
Category: Feedback. iOS 17.0+.
Files: RatingScrub.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add RatingScrub

A star rating you tap or scrub, with soft rounded stars that fill as solid blocks colored by the score, the star under your finger lifting, a staggered spring settle, and a light numeral with a label chip that morph as you go.

Tap-or-scrub star rating with lift, staggered settle, a score-colored fill, and an adjustable accessibility element.

### Notes

- Stars are soft rounded shapes that fill as solid blocks. The block follows the score through `Style.levels` (tangerine, sand, butter, sage, sky by default), so a low rating reads differently from a high one at a glance. Pass `tint` to use one color for every score.
- With `labels`, a caption sits under the stars: a light numeral with a dimmed decimal and "/ 5", and a solid chip with the label for the rounded-up rating. It spans the width of the stars and morphs as you scrub. Unrated shows "Tap or slide".
- One `DragGesture` with zero minimum distance handles tap and scrub. While the finger is down the star under it lifts on an interactive spring; on release the stars settle with a spring delayed by their distance from that star, so the release ripples outward.
- Haptics: `.selection` on each step, a rigid impact when the value hits 0 or the maximum.
- `isReadOnly` removes the gesture and the VoiceOver adjustable action but keeps the value readable. `size` scales with Dynamic Type.

### Parameters

- `rating`: Bound value from 0 to `count`, in whole or half steps.
- `count`: Number of stars.
- `allowsHalf`: Snap to half stars.
- `labels`: Optional one label per star ("Poor" ... "Great"). Adds a caption under the stars: a light numeral and a label chip for the rounded-up rating.
- `isReadOnly`: Shows the value without a gesture or adjustable action.
- `size`: Star point size; scales with Dynamic Type.
- `tint`: Overrides the fill color for every score. Defaults to `style.levels`, one block per score.
- `style`: Fill colors per score, the empty star color and text colors. `.standard` runs tangerine, sand, butter, sage, sky.

## Reaction Toggle (`ReactionToggle`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/feedback/reaction-toggle
Category: Feedback. iOS 17.0+.
Files: ReactionToggle.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add ReactionToggle

A like or save toggle that presses in, floods its capsule with a solid color block from the symbol outward, bounces the symbol, sends out one fading halo, and can roll a count or float a confirmation pill.

Reaction toggle with press feel, a circular block flood, a symbol bounce, one halo, and an optional count and pill.

### Notes

- At rest the toggle is a quiet capsule. Turning it on floods the capsule with a solid block that grows out of the symbol, swaps to the filled symbol in dark ink, bounces it with a small tilt, and sends one halo outward. Turning it off drains the block.
- `Style` holds the block (`fill`), its `ink`, the rest capsule colors and the pill colors, with house palette defaults that adapt to light and dark. `tint` still works and overrides `fill`. Set `isContained: false` for a bare symbol that fills like a sticker under an ink outline.
- The press state comes from a `ButtonStyle`, so it tracks the real touch: scale in stiffly, spring out on release.
- `count` is the base value from your model; the view adds one while `isOn` so the number rolls immediately without a round trip. `size` scales with Dynamic Type and the hit area never drops below 44 pt.
- `confirmation` floats a dark pill with a check above the toggle for 1.3 s.
- Under Reduce Motion the flood crossfades, and there is no bounce or halo; the haptic still fires on the off-to-on edge only.

### Parameters

- `isOn`: Bound reaction state.
- `systemImage`: Outline symbol name.
- `filledImage`: Filled symbol name; defaults to `systemImage` with `.fill` appended.
- `count`: Optional number shown beside the symbol; it rolls with `numericText` and offsets by one while `isOn`.
- `confirmation`: Optional pill text floated above the toggle when turned on, such as "Saved".
- `size`: Symbol point size; scales with Dynamic Type. The hit area is at least 44 pt.
- `tint`: Overrides the block color used when on. Defaults to `style.fill`.
- `style`: Colors and shape. `.standard` is a tangerine block with dark ink on a quiet capsule; set `isContained` to `false` for a bare symbol.

## Skeleton Loader (`SkeletonLoader`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/feedback/skeleton-loader
Category: Feedback. iOS 17.0+.
Files: SkeletonLoader.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add SkeletonLoader

Solid placeholder bones and a self-masking modifier that turns any layout, color blocks included, into one quiet shape sweeping a soft diagonal highlight on a shared clock, then hands off as content unblurs and rises row by row.

Standalone placeholder bone. Use `.skeleton(isLoading:)` to redact real content instead.

### Notes

- `.skeleton(isLoading:)` keeps the real view in the tree, hidden, so layout never jumps. The placeholder is a silhouette of the redacted view drawn through an alpha threshold, so text bars, color blocks and symbols all become one solid bone color, whatever colors the content uses.
- A soft diagonal highlight sweeps across the bones. Every instance reads the same reference clock, which keeps every skeleton on screen in phase.
- On handoff the placeholder fades while the content unblurs and rises 6 pt; `staggerIndex` delays that by 60 ms per row so lists reveal top to bottom.
- `isFailed` stops the sweep and dims the bones so the slot reads as empty; flip `isLoading` back on to retry.
- `Style` sets the bone `fill`, the sweep `highlight`, the `period` and the failed opacity, with house palette defaults that adapt to light and dark. Pass the same style to `SkeletonLoader` bones and `.skeleton` so they match.
- Reduce Transparency switches to an opaque fill without the sweep. Under Reduce Motion there is no sweep and the handoff is an instant swap.
- For a whole projects screen that starts as ghost rows and hands off to real content, see the Pro Projects screen.

### Parameters

- `shape`: `.rounded(radius)`, `.circle`, `.capsule`, or `.text(lines:)` for a stack of text lines with a shorter last line.
- `isFailed`: Stops the sweep and dims the bone so the slot reads as empty.
- `style`: Bone and highlight colors and the sweep period. `.standard` is a solid warm grey that adapts to light and dark.

## Status Morph (`StatusMorph`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/feedback/status-morph
Category: Feedback. iOS 17.0+.
Files: StatusMorph.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add StatusMorph

One continuous stroke that spins as a loading arc, closes into a ring, floods into a solid block and draws a check in dark ink on success, or a cross with a nudge on failure, with an optional morphing caption.

Idle, loading, success, and failure in one ring that lands as a solid block.

### Notes

- Loading is a 72% arc in ink rotated by a `TimelineView` clock, so nothing runs while idle. On success or failure the arc's current angle is captured and the ring closes from there, then a solid block floods out of it (sage for success, tangerine for failure) and the check or cross draws in dark ink.
- `Style` holds the two blocks, the ink, the arc and track colors and the caption colors, with house palette defaults that adapt to light and dark. `tint` still works and overrides the success block.
- The check and cross are one `Shape` with `trim`, so the cross draws its two lines in order. Failure adds a `.error` haptic and a short horizontal nudge via `keyframeAnimator`; success plays `.success` and an optional soft scale pop.
- A view that appears already settled shows its final block without replaying the morph.
- `size` is a `@ScaledMetric`, so the ring grows with Dynamic Type alongside its caption.
- Under Reduce Motion the arc does not spin, states crossfade, and the nudge and pop are skipped.
- For a full agent task screen with a live tool timeline, see the Pro Agent Task screen.

### Parameters

- `state`: `.idle`, `.loading`, `.success`, or `.failure`.
- `captions`: Optional caption per state shown under the ring, morphed with `.blurReplace`. Use `.saving` for "Saving / Saved / Failed".
- `size`: Ring diameter in points; scales with Dynamic Type.
- `lineWidth`: Stroke width for the ring, check, and cross.
- `tint`: Overrides the success block color. Defaults to `style.success`.
- `pops`: Soft scale pop when success lands.
- `style`: Block, stroke and caption colors. `.standard` lands sage for success and tangerine for failure, with dark ink marks.

## Glass Action Menu (`GlassActionMenu`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/glass/glass-action-menu
Category: Glass. iOS 17.0+. Liquid Glass on iOS 26 with a Material fallback.
Files: GlassActionMenu.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add GlassActionMenu

A floating signal trigger that long-presses open into a staggered line or arc of color-block actions you can slide across and release to fire; the trigger confirms with a check, tap toggles, a scrim dismisses, and the glass morphs on iOS 26.

Floating action menu with a hold-slide-release gesture, staggered emergence, a dimming scrim and a confirming trigger.

### Notes

- Two ways in: a tap toggles the menu, a 350ms hold expands it and keeps the same touch live, so you can slide across items (each crossing lifts the item and ticks `.selection`) and release to fire. Releasing a hold on empty space leaves the menu open.
- Items emerge one at a time (45ms stagger, reversed on collapse) and labels fade in only after the last item has landed. On iOS 26 each item carries a `glassEffectID` inside a `GlassEffectContainer`, so the glass blends with the trigger as it travels; earlier the same choreography runs on `.regularMaterial`.
- The scrim is an oversized background behind the trigger; it dims everything beneath the menu in its parent and dismisses on tap. Place the menu last in a `ZStack` so nothing sits above it.
- Phases: `collapsed`, `expanding`, `open`, `hovering`, `firing`, `collapsing`. Reduce Motion drops the stagger and the lift and crossfades instead; Reduce Transparency swaps glass and Material for opaque fills.
- VoiceOver sees the trigger as a button (double tap toggles) and each item as its own button while the menu is open.
- Items take an optional `tint` (`Item(symbol:label:tint:action:)`) and render as solid color blocks with dark ink; on iOS 26 clear glass sits on top for the edge and the morph. Untinted items stay glass.
- The trigger defaults to the house signal color with dark ink (`tint` is now optional; `nil` uses `Style.trigger`). After an action fires it shows a checkmark for 0.9s (`Style.confirmsAction`).
- `Style`: `trigger`, `ink`, `labelFill`, `labelInk` (solid label capsules), `triggerSize`, `itemSize`, `scrimOpacity`, `confirmsAction`. In an arc of three or more, the top item's label sits above it.
- For a floating pill that morphs into a full toolbar and panel, see the Pro Reader screen (`morph-nav`).

### Parameters

- `items`: Actions in emergence order (nearest to the trigger first). Give an item a `tint` to draw it as a color block.
- `triggerSymbol`: SF Symbol on the collapsed trigger. Rotates 45° while open.
- `arrangement`: `.linear` stacks items upward; `.arc` fans them from up to leading, for a bottom-trailing placement.
- `tint`: Trigger fill. `nil` uses `style.trigger`, the house signal color. Items keep their own tints so the trigger reads as the anchor.
- `isExpanded`: Optional binding to open or close the menu programmatically; it is written back when the user toggles it.
- `style`: Trigger and label colors, sizes, scrim strength and the confirmation check.

## Glass Segments (`GlassSegments`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/glass/glass-segments
Category: Glass. iOS 17.0+. Liquid Glass on iOS 26 with a Material fallback.
Files: GlassSegments.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add GlassSegments

A segmented control whose glass indicator you can grab and drag: it lifts under the finger, rubber-bands past the ends, stretches with velocity and settles with a spring, while the label ink flips exactly under its edge; tap still works.

Visual tuning for `GlassSegments`. `standard` is a solid track with a glass indicator; set `indicatorTint` for a color block indicator.

### Notes

- A touch that lands on the indicator grabs it: it lifts (scale 1.04, deeper shadow), follows the finger, rubber-bands up to one segment past either end and stretches along the drag with velocity. Release commits to the segment the flick would land on (`predictedEndLocation`) with a `.spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.3)`. A touch anywhere else is a plain tap on that segment.
- One `.selection` haptic fires each time the indicator's center crosses into a new segment, and once on tap; there is no second tick on release.
- Label emphasis is continuous: each label's opacity tracks how much of the indicator overlaps it, so the emphasis hands over during the drag instead of swapping at the end.
- Reduce Transparency swaps the track for an opaque system fill. Reduce Motion removes the stretch and the lift scale and shortens the settle.
- Segments share the width equally; the control fills its container, so constrain it with `.frame(width:)` when you want it compact.
- Labels are drawn twice: once in `Style.ink`, and once in `Style.selectedInk` masked to the indicator's live shape, so the color hands over exactly under the indicator edge while dragging or stretching.
- The indicator is a solid fill (`indicatorSurface`, or `indicatorTint` for a color block) under clear Liquid Glass on iOS 26, so it reads on the track in light and dark. `GlassSegmentsStyle.block(_:)` makes a block indicator with dark ink.
- `Style` (`GlassSegments.Style`, alias of `GlassSegmentsStyle`): `track`, `ink`, `selectedInk`, `indicatorTint`, `indicatorSurface`, `font`, `disabledOpacity`. `.disabled(true)` fades the control and ignores touches. The row height scales with Dynamic Type (capped at 1.5x).
- For a floating tab bar whose lens follows the finger, see the Pro Lessons screen (`lens-tab-bar`).

## Glass Surface (`GlassSurface`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/glass/glass-surface
Category: Glass. iOS 17.0+. Liquid Glass on iOS 26 with a Material fallback.
Files: GlassSurface.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add GlassSurface

The Glass family foundation: Liquid Glass in a capsule, rect, circle or concentric shape on iOS 26, with a layered Material fallback that keeps the press response, solid tint, specular edge and a designed disabled state everywhere else.

Liquid Glass on iOS 26, a layered Material surface everywhere else, with the same press feel on both.

### Notes

- On iOS 26 this is real `.glassEffect(_:in:)`; earlier, or under Reduce Transparency, it is `.regularMaterial` (opaque `secondarySystemBackground` under Reduce Transparency) with a top light, a two-layer soft shadow and a specular edge: a bright top highlight plus a faint `.primary` edge.
- `interactive: true` keeps the press feel on the fallback: scale `Style.pressedScale` (0.96), a brighten pass and a light impact. The press is tracked with a simultaneous gesture, so a `Button` inside still owns the tap. Reduce Motion drops the scale but keeps the brighten and haptic.
- `.concentric(minimum:)` resolves to `ConcentricRectangle` on iOS 26 (set `.containerShape` on the parent) and to a continuous rounded rect with `minimum` as the radius earlier.
- `GlassSurface.Group(spacing:)` is `GlassEffectContainer` on iOS 26 so neighbouring surfaces blend where they meet; earlier it is a transparent wrapper.
- `Style` (`.standard`): `tintAmount` (0.72, so a tinted fallback reads as a color block), `specular`, `shadow`, `pressedScale` (0.96), `disabledOpacity` and `solidFill` for Reduce Transparency.
- Disabled: `.disabled(true)` fades and desaturates the surface and silences the press response on both paths.
- For a floating glass card over full-bleed art with detents, see the Pro Stay screen (`glass-sheet`).

### Parameters

- `shape`: `.capsule`, `.rect(cornerRadius:)`, `.circle` or `.concentric(minimum:)` (iOS 26 concentric corners, continuous corners earlier).
- `tint`: Optional tint. Glass tints natively; the fallback lays it over the Material at `style.tintAmount`, so it reads as a color block.
- `interactive`: Press response: system glass on iOS 26; on the fallback the surface scales to `style.pressedScale`, brightens and plays a light impact.
- `style`: Fallback tint strength, specular edge, depth shadow, press scale, disabled opacity and the Reduce Transparency fill.

## Amount Field (`AmountField`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/inputs/amount-field
Category: Inputs. iOS 17.0+.
Files: AmountField.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add AmountField

A currency amount entry that formats live in the user's locale as each digit lands (grouping, decimal separator, symbol before or after, the currency's own fraction digits), with a large auto-fitting figure whose digits roll in, a blinking caret right after the digits, robust paste of amounts like "$1,234.56" or "1 234,56 €", and a limit that refuses the keystroke with a damped shake, an error haptic and a message line, all backed by a `Decimal` binding.

Currency amount entry with live locale formatting, a `Decimal` value and a limit. The field keeps its own digit buffer and renders the formatted string itself, so the caret never jumps and locale separators never break parsing. Formatting follows `\.locale`; fraction digits come from the currency.

### Notes

- The field keeps its own buffer of typed digits and renders the formatted string itself. A hidden `TextField` with `.decimalPad` captures keys, so the caret never jumps and grouping separators never reach a parser. The caret is drawn right after the digits, before a trailing symbol ("1.234,56| €").
- The value is a `Decimal`. Fraction digits come from the currency through `Decimal.FormatStyle.Currency`: JPY takes none, USD two, KWD three. Formatting follows `\.locale`, so `.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: "de_DE"))` gives "1.234,56 €", en_IN groups in lakhs ("₹1,23,456") and ar_SA shows Arabic-Indic digits.
- While typing, what you typed is what you see: "12." keeps its separator and "12.50" keeps its zero. Leading zeros are stripped, "." on an empty field starts "0.", a second separator is ignored and digits past the currency's precision are dropped. Leaving the field settles "12.5" to "12.50" and "12." to "12".
- Both "." and "," (and the Arabic decimal separator) work as the decimal key, whatever the device region. Digits in any script are accepted and stored as ASCII.
