- Paste (long-press, or Command-V) parses "1,234.56", "$99", "1 234,56 €", "US$ 12" and Arabic-Indic text. A lone separator followed by exactly three digits reads as thousands unless the currency has three decimals. Words, two numbers or a minus sign are rejected with an error haptic.
- `limit` refuses the keystroke or paste that would pass it: a damped shake, an `.error` haptic, a VoiceOver announcement and the `limitMessage` line, which fades after a moment. An external value over the limit is shown in `Style.error` with the message, not clamped.
- External writes to the binding (a quick-amount chip, a reset) redraw the display at the currency's precision. Negative or over-precise values are normalized and written back.
- `.hero` is a large light figure that scales down to fit its width, with digits rolling in through `.numericText()`. `.compact` is a 56pt block with a focus ring. Both follow Dynamic Type.
- VoiceOver reads the label and the full formatted amount as the value ("$1,234.56"), and the limit as a hint. `.disabled(true)` dims the field and blocks focus. `isFocused` lets you raise or dismiss the keyboard.
- Reduce Motion: no shake (the digits flash `Style.error` instead), and digit changes crossfade.

### Parameters

- `label`: Caption above the amount, also the accessibility label. Pass an empty string to hide the caption.
- `value`: Bound amount. Never negative; external values are shown at the currency's precision (a negative or over-precise value is normalized and written back).
- `currencyCode`: ISO 4217 code. Sets the symbol and the fraction digits (USD 2, JPY 0, KWD 3). Defaults to the current locale's currency.
- `limit`: Largest amount that can be typed or pasted. A keystroke past it is refused with a shake (a color flash under Reduce Motion), an error haptic and the limit message. `nil` means no limit.
- `limitMessage`: Line shown when the limit refuses input or the value is over it. `nil` shows "Up to" plus the formatted limit; an empty string shows no line.
- `allowsDecimal`: Allow the decimal key. When `false`, amounts are whole units and the number pad has no decimal key.
- `size`: `.hero` is a large centered figure for a payments screen; `.compact` is a 56pt form-row block.
- `isFocused`: Optional binding to read or drive keyboard focus, for example to raise the keyboard on appear.
- `style`: Colors and metrics. Defaults to the Swift Pieces house palette, adapting to light and dark.

## Date Range Picker (`DateRangePicker`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/inputs/date-range-picker
Category: Inputs. iOS 17.0+.
Files: DateRangePicker.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add DateRangePicker

A start-to-end date range picker on a paged month grid built from the environment calendar and locale, where the first tap drops a solid butter start block, the second closes the range and a soft band sweeps day by day between the two blocks, wrapping across week rows with rounded caps, while sold-out days are struck through, a maximum length dims unreachable days, months page by swipe or chevrons with a rolling title, and a summary reads out the dates and nights.

Day-granular start/end range picker with a paged month grid. The selection is always two start-of-day dates in the environment `Calendar` and `TimeZone` (`upperBound` is the start of the last day, e.g. the check-out day for a stay). The first tap sets a start, the second closes the range (a day before the start becomes the new start), and a third tap starts over. A range can never contain a disabled or out-of-bounds day: an end tap that would span one, or that exceeds `maximumLength`, is refused with an error haptic and a short notice, and the start stays in place.

### Notes

- The selection is a `ClosedRange<Date>` of start-of-day dates in the environment `Calendar` and `TimeZone`. `upperBound` is the start of the last day (the check-out day for a stay). Dates you pass in are normalized to their day.
- First tap sets the start and clears any old range, second tap sets the end, third tap starts a new range. Tapping a day before the pending start moves the start there. In `.nights` mode tapping the start again cancels it; in `.days` mode it confirms a one-day range.
- A range never contains an unavailable day. An end tap that would span a day marked by `isDateDisabled` or outside `bounds`, or that exceeds `maximumLength`, is refused: the start stays, an `.error` haptic plays, and a notice chip ("Includes unavailable dates", "Up to 14 nights") replaces the length chip for two seconds. While a start is pending, days that cannot close the range are dimmed.
- The grid comes from the calendar: `firstWeekday`, days per week, days in the month and the weekday offset all come from `Calendar` APIs, so Hebrew, Islamic, Ethiopic and other calendars lay out correctly. Weekday symbols are the calendar's very short standalone symbols; day numbers, month titles and the summary use `Date.FormatStyle` and `Date.IntervalFormatStyle` in the environment locale, including native digits.
- Day math uses `Calendar.date(byAdding:)` and counts days on civil dates, never 86,400 second steps, so 23 and 25 hour DST days and time zones whose midnight is skipped stay exact.
- The band is drawn per cell as half-cell pieces under the endpoint blocks, so it reads as one strip that wraps across week rows with rounded caps at row edges and at month edges. When a range completes it sweeps in from the start, one day at a time. `UnevenRoundedRectangle` uses leading and trailing radii, so caps mirror in right-to-left layouts, where the grid also flows right to left.
- Months page with the chevrons or a horizontal swipe (a paging `ScrollView`), and the title rolls in the paging direction. Paging stops at the months of `bounds`; without bounds it spans five years either side of today and the selection's month.
- The summary shows the range in the locale's interval pattern ("Mar 4 – 9") and a length chip in `counting` units, pluralized with automatic grammar agreement.
- Haptics: `.selection` when a start is set, `.success` when a range completes, `.error` on a refused end.
- VoiceOver: each day is a button labeled with its full date ("Tuesday, March 4", plus the year outside the current one, and "Today" first for today), with the `.isSelected` trait inside the range and a value of Start date, End date, In range or Unavailable. Month changes, completed ranges and refusals are announced.
- Dynamic Type: day cells grow with `@ScaledMetric` from 44pt up to 76pt tall; day numbers scale to accessibility sizes and shrink to fit rather than clip. The summary stacks when it no longer fits on one line.
- Reduce Motion: no sweep, springs or rolling title. The swipe no longer slides the grid; both the swipe and the chevrons crossfade to the next month.
- `Style` sets the ground, day text, muted text, band, endpoint blocks, ink on blocks, the today dot, disabled days, the month buttons, the notice chip and the corner radius. `.disabled(true)` dims the picker and stops taps and paging.
- For booking a time slot inside a day, see the slot picker in Swift Pieces Pro.

### Parameters

- `selection`: Bound range, or `nil` while nothing (or only a start) is chosen. In `.nights` mode it stays `nil` until the end is tapped; in `.days` mode a lone start already reads as a one-day range.
- `bounds`: First and last selectable days. Days outside are muted and inert, and paging stops at their months. `nil` allows any day and pages five years either side of today.
- `isDateDisabled`: Marks single days unavailable (for example sold-out nights). Called with the start of each day; unavailable days are struck through and can never be inside a range.
- `maximumLength`: Longest allowed range, counted in `counting` units. While a start is pending, days that cannot close the range are dimmed.
- `counting`: `.days` counts both ends (Mar 4 to Mar 9 is 6 days, and a single day is allowed). `.nights` counts nights (5 nights, and the end must be after the start).
- `showsSummary`: Show the header line with the formatted range and its length chip.
- `style`: Colors and corner radius. Defaults to the Swift Pieces house palette (butter endpoint blocks with dark ink on a soft butter band), adapting to light and dark.

## Expanding Track (`ExpandingTrack`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/inputs/expanding-track
Category: Inputs. iOS 17.0+.
Files: ExpandingTrack.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add ExpandingTrack

A thumbless slider drawn as a solid color bar that swells from 8pt to a 32pt block under the finger, shows detent dots and an inverting readout while dragging, squishes past either end, and can carry an uppercase label with a big light numeral; a second init selects a range with two sinking handles.

Thumbless slider that swells into a solid block on touch. Bind a `Double` for a single value or a `ClosedRange<Double>` for a range.

### Notes

- There is no thumb: the whole 44pt row is the hit area and the value follows the finger's x position directly, so the bar can rest at 8pt and still be easy to grab. While dragging it swells to a 32pt block (`Style.activeHeight`) with detent dots at each `step` and a soft shadow.
- Pass `title` for the labeled layout: an uppercase caption with the value as a big light numeral above the track, decimals dimmed at the locale's separator. Without a title the value prints inside the block while dragging, drawn twice so it switches to `ink` where the fill passes under it.
- Dragging past either end squishes the track toward the far edge with a rubber-band curve (asymptote 22pt) and fires a rigid impact once when the value hits the bound; release springs it back.
- Selection ticks fire per `step` crossing, or every tenth of the span when there is no step; the optional symbol plays `.variableColor` only when the value rises past a tick.
- The range init keeps the handles apart by `minimumDistance` and lets the active ink handle sink into the block; VoiceOver gets separate "Minimum" and "Maximum" adjustable elements, prefixed with the title when there is one.
- `Style` carries the trough, the fill block, ink, labels and track metrics. `.standard` is the house palette (tangerine on a quiet trough); pass `.init(fill:)` to use another block. `.disabled(true)` greys the fill.
- Reduce Motion: the track does not swell and the readout appears above its trailing end instead of inside it.

### Parameters

- `value`: Bound single value (single-value init).
- `range`: Bound selected range (range init). The two handles never cross.
- `bounds`: Minimum and maximum selectable values.
- `step`: Optional snapping increment. Also sets the spacing of the selection ticks and detent dots; without it, ticks fire every tenth of the span.
- `minimumDistance`: Smallest gap the range handles keep between them (range init only).
- `symbol`: Optional leading SF Symbol that plays a variable-color pulse each time the value rises past a tick.
- `title`: Optional label. Shows an uppercase caption with the value as a big light numeral above the track (decimals dimmed), and becomes the VoiceOver label.
- `style`: Colors and track metrics. Defaults to the Swift Pieces house palette, adapting to light and dark.
- `format`: Formats the readout and the VoiceOver value. Defaults to up to two decimals.

## Filter Rail (`FilterRail`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/inputs/filter-rail
Category: Inputs. iOS 17.0+.
Files: FilterRail.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add FilterRail

A scrolling rail of filter chips with optional counts where one solid indicator glides between single-select picks, multi-select picks light up as color blocks with dark ink and gather at the leading edge behind a counting Clear chip, the chosen chip scrolls into view, and edges fade only when content overflows.

Horizontal chip rail bound to a `Set` of selected titles.

### Notes

- Single-select uses one `matchedGeometryEffect` capsule in `Style.indicator` that glides from the previous chip to the new one; tapping the selected chip again keeps it selected, so include an "All" option if you need a neutral state.
- Multi-select turns each picked chip into a solid block with a check. Colors come from `Style.blocks` by option position, so a chip keeps its color wherever it moves. Picks gather at the leading edge behind a Clear chip that counts them.
- `counts` adds a result count after each title; VoiceOver reads it as the chip's value.
- Selection changes set `scrollPosition(id:)`, so the chosen chip centers itself (single) or the rail returns to its leading edge (multi).
- Edge fades are computed from the content frame in a named coordinate space, so they show only on the side that actually has chips hidden.
- Chips press to 0.96 with a fast press-in and springy release; `.disabled(true)` dims the whole rail. A selection haptic fires on every change to the bound set.
- For a searchable list of commands instead of a rail, see the Command Palette screen in Swift Pieces Pro.

### Parameters

- `options`: Chip titles, in order.
- `selection`: Selected titles. Single-select keeps exactly one once anything is chosen.
- `allowsMultiple`: Allow several chips at once. Selected chips move to the leading edge and a Clear chip appears.
- `counts`: Optional result count per title, shown after the chip title and read by VoiceOver.
- `style`: Colors and chip height. Defaults to the Swift Pieces house palette, adapting to light and dark.

## Form Field (`FormField`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/inputs/form-field
Category: Inputs. iOS 17.0+.
Files: FormField.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add FormField

A text field on a soft 56pt block whose label rests inside as a placeholder and glides up into a caption on focus or once filled, with an optional leading icon, a clear button, help text, a grapheme-accurate character limit with a counter that turns into a tangerine chip and bumps when extra input is refused, and validation that waits until you leave the field before drawing an error ring, sliding in the message with an error haptic and a VoiceOver announcement, then shows a sage check once fixed.

Text field with a floating label, help and error text, a character limit and a counter. Chain fields by applying `.focused($focus, equals: .email)` to each `FormField` (focus reaches the text field inside) and moving focus in `onSubmit`. Apply ``SwiftUI/View/formFieldRevealsErrors(_:)`` to a form to show every field's validation at once, for example after a submit button is tapped.

### Notes

- The label is one `Text` in `.body` that moves between two alignments and scales down into a reserved caption slot. The scale is the caption-to-body line-height ratio at the current Dynamic Type size, so the label lands in the same place at every size, including the accessibility sizes, with no font swap and no jump.
- `prompt` shows only while the field is focused and empty, under the floated label. The system placeholder is suppressed so the label is never drawn twice.
- `limit` counts extended grapheme clusters (`String.count`), so a flag, a family emoji or a letter with a combining accent is one character. Typing or pasting past the limit trims with `prefix(limit)`, which never cuts a character in half. A refused keystroke fires a light impact and bumps the counter. At the limit the counter becomes a solid `Style.error` chip with ink text.
- The counter is `count/limit` with localized digits. With an IME that composes text (Japanese, Chinese), trimming can end a composition early when it runs past the limit.
- Validation timing: `.onBlur` (default) waits until the field has been edited and left, `.onSubmit` waits for Return, `.live` starts with the first edit. After that the field validates on every keystroke, so the error clears the moment the text is fixed and a sage check appears. An `error` passed from outside shows immediately and takes priority.
- `formFieldRevealsErrors(true)` on a container arms every field inside, for a Save button that should flag untouched required fields.
- When an error first appears the ring turns `Style.error`, the message slides in under the field with an exclamation glyph, and an `.error` haptic plays once. Help text returns when the error clears.
- Focus: apply `.focused($focus, equals: .email)` to the `FormField` itself and move focus in `onSubmit`, with `submitLabel: .next`. Tapping anywhere on the block, including the icon and padding, focuses the field. The clear button appears while focused and non-empty and keeps the keyboard up.
- `axis: .vertical` grows up to eight lines. Return inserts a newline there, so `onSubmit` does not fire; put a multiline field last in a chain.
- `.emailAddress` and `.URL` keyboards (and email, URL and username content types) turn off autocapitalization and autocorrection.
- VoiceOver reads the label, the text with the counter ("12 of 160 characters") as the value, and the error or help as the hint. A new or changed error is announced. The floating label, icon, check and footer are hidden to avoid double reading.
- `Style` sets the field, label, secondary, focus ring, error, success and ink colors plus minimum height (44pt floor) and corner radius. `.disabled(true)` dims the field and hides the clear button.
- Reduce Motion: the label still moves (it is the state change) but on a short ease with no bounce, messages crossfade instead of sliding, and the counter changes color without the bump.

### Parameters

- `label`: The label. Rests inside the empty field as its placeholder, floats up into a caption on focus or once filled, and is the accessibility label.
- `text`: Bound text.
- `prompt`: Placeholder shown under the floated label only while the field is focused and empty, e.g. "you@example.com".
- `help`: Supporting text below the field, shown whenever there is no error. Also the VoiceOver hint.
- `leading`: Icon at the leading edge, e.g. `Image(systemName: "envelope")`.
- `limit`: Maximum length in characters (extended grapheme clusters, so an emoji or accented letter counts as one). Typing or pasting past it is trimmed without splitting a character, and a "12/50" counter appears.
- `axis`: `.horizontal` for one line; `.vertical` for a multiline field that grows up to eight lines, where Return inserts a newline.
- `validation`: When `validate` starts running. `.onBlur` (default) waits until the field has been edited and left once, then validates live. `.onSubmit` waits for Return. `.live` starts with the first edit.
- `validate`: Returns an error message for invalid text, or `nil` when valid. A sage check appears once the text is valid.
- `error`: An error from outside the field (e.g. "Email already in use" from a server). Shown immediately and ahead of `validate`.
- `textContentType`: Autofill hint, e.g. `.emailAddress`, `.name`, `.oneTimeCode`.
- `keyboardType`: Keyboard. `.emailAddress` and `.URL` also turn off autocapitalization and autocorrection.
- `submitLabel`: The Return key label, e.g. `.next` or `.done`.
- `onSubmit`: Called when Return is pressed in a one-line field. Move focus to the next field here.
- `style`: Colors and field metrics. Defaults to the Swift Pieces house palette, adapting to light and dark.

## Range Slider (`RangeSlider`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/inputs/range-slider
Category: Inputs. iOS 17.0+.
Files: RangeSlider.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add RangeSlider

A dual-thumb slider for a range of values, with two round thumbs on a quiet track and the selected span drawn as a solid color block between them; drag either thumb or touch the track to pull the nearest one over, values snap to a step without floating drift, the thumbs never cross and keep a minimum gap, a grabbed thumb grows and its readout chip fills with the block color, the two readouts merge into one chip instead of colliding, and every step ticks a selection haptic with a firmer impact at a bound or the gap.

Dual-thumb slider that binds a `ClosedRange` of any floating-point type. The simplest call is one line: `RangeSlider(value: $price, in: 0...1000, step: 10, format: .currency(code: "USD").precision(.fractionLength(0)))`. Pass a `FormatStyle` or a `(V) -> String` closure as `format`; it drives the readouts and the VoiceOver values.

### Notes

- Generic over any `BinaryFloatingPoint` (`Double`, `Float`, `CGFloat`). Bind a `ClosedRange`; pass `format:` as a `FormatStyle` (`.currency(code: "USD").precision(.fractionLength(0))`, `.percent`) or a `(V) -> String` closure. The format drives the readouts and the VoiceOver values.
- Drag either thumb, or touch the track and the nearest thumb glides to the finger. Grabbing a thumb keeps the finger's offset, so it never jumps under the touch. When both thumbs sit on the same point, the first clear movement decides: right (in left-to-right) takes the upper thumb, left takes the lower.
- The thumbs never cross. They stop `minimumDistance` apart, kept on the step grid (a 5 gap with step 10 stops at 10).
- `step` snaps from `bounds.lowerBound`. Both bounds stay reachable when the span is not a multiple of the step (0...1000 by 30 reaches 1000). Values are rounded to the step's decimal places, so `0.1` steps write `0.3`, not `0.30000000000000004`. Out-of-bounds or reversed bindings are shown clamped and written back clean on the first change.
- Readouts: `.thumbs` (default) floats a chip over each thumb, clamped inside the track; when the two would come within 6pt they crossfade into one "lower – upper" chip. A grabbed thumb grows and its chip fills with the block color. `.header` prints "lower – upper" above the track and stacks the values at large text sizes. `.hidden` shows nothing.
- Haptics: `.selection` on each value change while dragging (every 5% of the span without a step), throttled to about 30 per second; a rigid `.impact` once when a thumb reaches a bound or the minimum gap.
- Right-to-left: the track mirrors, so the lower thumb sits on the right, and the merged chip reads in the reader's direction.
- VoiceOver: two adjustable elements, "Minimum" then "Maximum" (set `lowerLabel` and `upperLabel`, e.g. "Minimum price"). Swipe up or down moves one `step` to the next valid value, or 1% of the span without a step.
- Thumbs keep a 44pt touch and VoiceOver target even when `Style.thumbSize` draws them smaller. Readouts use text styles and grow with Dynamic Type.
- `Style` sets the track, the fill block, thumb face and border, ink, labels, chips, track height and thumb size. `.disabled(true)` desaturates, dims and blocks input.
- Reduce Motion: no spring, no thumb growth (the border still thickens), and the thumbs follow the finger without smoothing.
- The drag starts on touch-down so the track responds to taps; inside a vertical `ScrollView` or sheet, a drag that begins on the slider moves the slider rather than scrolling.
- For a full filter sheet built around it, see the filter sheet in Swift Pieces Pro.

### Parameters

- `value`: Bound selected range. Values outside `bounds` are shown clamped; the first change writes a clean, in-bounds range back.
- `bounds`: Minimum and maximum selectable values. Both are always reachable, even when the span is not a multiple of `step`.
- `step`: Optional snapping increment, measured from `bounds.lowerBound`. Snapped values are rounded to the step's decimal places, so `0.1` steps give `0.3`, never `0.30000000000000004`. Without a step the values are continuous.
- `minimumDistance`: Smallest gap the two values keep. The thumbs stop against each other at this distance instead of crossing. Capped at the width of `bounds`.
- `readout`: Where the values print: `.thumbs` (chips above each thumb that merge into one when they would touch), `.header` (a "lower – upper" line above the track), or `.hidden`.
- `lowerLabel`: VoiceOver label of the lower thumb. Defaults to "Minimum".
- `upperLabel`: VoiceOver label of the upper thumb. Defaults to "Maximum".
- `style`: Colors and metrics. Defaults to the Swift Pieces house palette (a tangerine block on a quiet track), adapting to light and dark.
- `format`: Turns a value into the text shown in the readouts and spoken by VoiceOver. A `FormatStyle` (such as `.currency(code:)` or `.percent`) or a closure. Defaults to a plain number with as many decimals as `step` has (up to two without a step).

## Scrub Stepper (`ScrubStepper`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/inputs/scrub-stepper
Category: Inputs. iOS 17.0+.
Files: ScrubStepper.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add ScrubStepper

A capsule stepper with round minus and plus buttons around a solid numeral block; tap, hold to repeat with acceleration, or scrub sideways across the block for velocity-scaled steps while a ruler slides under the finger, and the capsule rubber-bands at the bounds.

Minus/plus stepper with hold-to-repeat and a horizontal scrub gesture.

### Notes

- One `DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)` covers the whole capsule and decides by start location: the round buttons at each end press, the numeral block in the middle starts a scrub. A press that moves more than 14pt sideways becomes a scrub; one that leaves the capsule by more than 20pt cancels without stepping.
- Pressed buttons invert (glyph color fills the circle) and shrink to 0.86; a button at its bound dims.
- Hold-to-repeat starts after 400ms and accelerates from 100ms to 60ms after 1.5s and 30ms after 3s. It runs in a `Task` that is cancelled on release, on cancel, on disappear, and when a bound is hit.
- Scrubbing consumes one step per 14pt of travel, multiplied by a velocity gain of up to 4x. While scrubbing the block widens and a ruler slides along its bottom edge with the finger. Scrub steps fire `.selection`; taps and repeats fire `.increase`/`.decrease`.
- At a bound the capsule nudges 6pt in the attempted direction with a rigid impact and springs back on release.
- `Style` sets the trough, buttons, glyph, the numeral block and its ink, and the height (44pt minimum, 52pt by default). `.standard` uses the butter block; pass `.init(block:)` for another.
- Supply an `.accessibilityLabel`; the value and adjustable action are provided. Reduce Motion drops the press scale, the widening and the nudge but keeps the rolling digits.

### Parameters

- `value`: Bound integer value.
- `range`: Allowed values. Pushing past a bound nudges the capsule 6pt and fires a rigid impact instead of moving.
- `step`: Amount added or removed per tap, repeat tick, or scrub unit.
- `style`: Colors and size. Defaults to the Swift Pieces house palette (a butter numeral block with dark ink), adapting to light and dark.

## Secure Entry (`SecureEntry`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/inputs/secure-entry
Category: Inputs. iOS 17.0+.
Files: SecureEntry.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add SecureEntry

A password field on a soft 56pt block with a focus ring and a round reveal toggle that keeps focus, a strength bar that grows through four color blocks with a matching label chip, requirement chips that turn into solid blocks with drawn checks and collapse when complete, a success check, and a damped shake with an error chip.

Password field with strength meter, live requirements, and inline error.

### Notes

- Revealing swaps `SecureField` for `TextField`; the toggle re-targets `@FocusState` to the new field so the keyboard stays up.
- The field is a soft 56pt block with no border at rest. Focus draws a 2pt ring in the label color; an `error` turns it to `Style.error`.
- Setting `error` triggers a damped four-cycle shake, an `.error` haptic, and slides an error chip in below. Clearing it slides the chip out.
- The strength bar grows through four blocks (tangerine, butter, sky, sage by default) with a matching WEAK / FAIR / GOOD / STRONG chip.
- Requirement chips appear while focused or filled. A met requirement becomes a sage block whose check draws in after the fill lands, with a `.selection` haptic. When all four pass, the chips collapse, a check appears in the field and a `.success` haptic plays.
- `Style` sets every color plus field height and radius. `.disabled(true)` dims the field.
- Reduce Motion: no shake, and every transition becomes an opacity fade.
- For one-time codes after sign-in, see the Verify screen (code entry) in Swift Pieces Pro.

### Parameters

- `label`: Static caption above the field, also the placeholder and accessibility label.
- `text`: Bound password text.
- `error`: Validation message. Setting it non-nil shakes the field, fires an error haptic, and slides an error chip in below.
- `showsStrength`: Show the strength bar and its label chip once text is non-empty.
- `showsRequirements`: Show the 8+ / number / symbol / mixed-case chips while focused or filled; they collapse once all four pass and a check appears in the field.
- `style`: Colors and field metrics. Defaults to the Swift Pieces house palette, adapting to light and dark.

## Token Field (`TokenField`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/inputs/token-field
Category: Inputs. iOS 17.0+.
Files: TokenField.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add TokenField

A tag and recipient field where committed entries become solid color chips with dark ink that wrap across lines while the text field takes the rest of the last line, return, comma or a paste of a whole list commits trimmed tokens with duplicate, limit and validation checks, backspace on an empty field highlights the last chip and a second press removes it, and an inline suggestion list filters as you type.

Wrapping token entry bound to an array of strings: tags, skills, recipients.

### Notes

- Chips and the input sit in a private wrapping `Layout`: leading-aligned rows, spacing that scales with Dynamic Type, and the input taking the rest of the last line. When that is narrower than the input's minimum (88pt, scaled) or its typed text, the input wraps to a new full-width line. A chip wider than the field truncates in the middle.
- Return, comma (including the full-width `，` and `、`) and pasted line breaks commit the trimmed text by default. `separators` adds `.semicolon` and `.space` for recipient lists. Pasting `a, b, c` adds three tokens in one animated change.
- Every entry is checked in order: `maxTokens`, then duplicates (case-insensitive, the first spelling is kept and the existing chip is highlighted), then `validate`. Rejected entries stay in the input so they can be fixed, with a damped shake, an error ring and an `.error` haptic.
- Backspace on an empty input highlights the last chip with a soft impact; a second backspace removes it with a rigid impact. Tapping a chip highlights it the same way. A zero-width space kept in front of the typed text makes this reliable on the software keyboard, where iOS reports no key event for backspace on an empty field. It is never shown or committed.
- The input uses a vertical-axis `TextField`, so return inserts a line break the field turns into a commit and the keyboard stays up between tokens. Valid text left in the input is committed quietly when the field loses focus.
- Suggestions appear under the field while typing, matched case- and diacritic-insensitively, prefix matches first, at most five, with the matched run in bold and a dot in the color the chip will take. Tokens already added are left out.
- Each token keeps the same chip color wherever it appears, picked from its text, so removing one never recolors the rest. Pass a single color in `Style.chips` for uniform chips.
- At `maxTokens` the input stops accepting text and shows a quiet count such as `5/5`. Backspace still removes.
- Tapping anywhere in the field that is not a chip focuses the input. Keyboard type, capitalization and content type pass through: apply `.keyboardType(.emailAddress)` and friends to the `TokenField`.
- VoiceOver: each chip is one element read as "Swift, token" with a Remove action; the input's label carries the placeholder and the token count; adds, removals and rejections are announced.
- `Style` sets the field, chip colors, ink, label, placeholder, error, corner radius and minimum height. `.disabled(true)` dims the field and disables removal.
- Reduce Motion: no shake or scale; chips and the suggestion list fade.

### Parameters

- `placeholder`: Shown in the input while it is empty, and the input's accessibility label.
- `tokens`: Bound tokens, in order. Changes from outside animate in and out like typed ones.
- `suggestions`: Candidates listed under the field while typing, matched case- and diacritic-insensitively (prefix matches first, then contains), excluding tokens already added.
- `maxTokens`: Upper limit. When reached the input stops accepting text and shows a quiet count such as "5/5"; backspace still removes.
- `allowsDuplicates`: When `false`, an entry that matches an existing token case-insensitively is not added; the existing chip is highlighted instead and the first spelling is kept.
- `separators`: Keys and characters that commit the typed text. `.standard` is return, comma and pasted line breaks. Full-width commas and semicolons count as their ASCII forms.
- `style`: Colors and field metrics. Defaults to the Swift Pieces house palette, adapting to light and dark.
- `validate`: Accepts or rejects a trimmed entry (for example an email check). A rejected entry stays in the input, the field shakes and an error haptic plays.

## Depth Carousel (`DepthCarousel`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/lists/depth-carousel
Category: Lists. iOS 17.0+.
Files: DepthCarousel.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add DepthCarousel

Paged cards that recede in depth as they leave center and hand each page a phase value for inner parallax. Neighbors come forward on tap, and a page counter sits beside a scrubbable pill indicator computed in absolute page coordinates so it never jumps.

Centered paging carousel with depth recession, per-page parallax phase, and a progress-linked indicator.

### Notes

- Snapping uses `.scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned)` with content margins sized so the aligned page is centered; the first and last pages center too. Fractional progress is read from the page row's position in the `.scrollView` coordinate space, so it works on iOS 17 without `onScrollGeometryChange`.
- Depth is driven by the same progress: pages shrink by `style.recede`, fade by `style.dim`, and their shadow gets lighter and leans back toward the centered page as they leave center. The `phase` handed to your content is -1...1, for inner parallax; the example drifts a cropped ink disc by `phase * 40` inside a solid color card. Under Reduce Motion the phase is 0 and only the dim remains.
- Tap a neighbor page to bring it to center; the centered page keeps its own gestures.
- Under the pages, a "01 / 04" counter (current page in rounded semibold, total dimmed, rolling as it changes) sits at the page's leading edge, and the pill track sits at its trailing edge. The pill is positioned in absolute page coordinates, so it tracks the finger and never jumps when a page settles; it widens while dragging. The whole 44pt-tall track is scrubbable, with a selection haptic per page.
- `Style` (`DepthCarousel.Style`, also `DepthCarouselStyle`): `recede`, `dim`, `shadowOpacity`, `indicatorActive`, `indicatorInactive`, `showsCounter`.
- VoiceOver treats the carousel as one container that reads "Page x of y" and supports swipe up/down to change pages; the indicator is hidden from it.
- `scrollClipDisabled()` lets neighbor pages peek past the carousel's own bounds, so give it full width.
- Want blur-and-tone depth, pinch peek-zoom and a full album screen? That is the Depth Gallery screen in Swift Pieces Pro.

### Parameters

- `data`: Identifiable collection of pages.
- `itemWidth`: Width of each page. Pages are centered in the carousel.
- `spacing`: Gap between pages.
- `showsIndicator`: Show the counter and pill indicator under the carousel. The pill track is scrubbable.
- `selection`: Optional binding to the centered element's id, for reading the page or moving programmatically.
- `style`: Depth amounts, indicator colors and whether the page counter shows. Defaults to the house palette.
- `content`: Builds one page from an element and its phase: 0 at center, -1 one page toward the leading edge, 1 toward the trailing edge. Use it for inner parallax, for example `.offset(x: phase * 24)` on a shape inside a clipped card.

## Paged List (`PagedList`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/lists/paged-list
Category: Lists. iOS 17.0+.
Files: PagedList.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add PagedList

An async/await infinite-scroll list that prefetches the next page a few rows before the end, never runs two loads at once, drops duplicate ids across pages, ignores stale responses after a refresh or cancel, shows pulsing skeleton rows, a footer spinner, an inline "Couldn't load more" chip with a solid Retry block that keeps loaded rows, a quiet "You're all caught up" footer, and pull to refresh that replaces rows only on success.

One page from your API: the rows it returned and the cursor for the page after it (`nil` when this was the last page). `Cursor` can be a page number, an offset, or an opaque token from your backend.

### Notes

- `load` receives `nil` for the first page, then each page's `next` cursor, which can be a page number, an offset or an opaque token. Return `PagedListPage(items:next:)` with `next: nil` on the last page. For page-number APIs, `PagedList(pageSize:)` builds the cursor for you and ends the list at the first short or empty page.
- The next page starts when the row `prefetchDistance` (5) rows from the end appears, or when the footer is on screen, so short pages keep loading until the screen fills. Only one load runs at a time; extra triggers are ignored.
- Items whose `id` has already been seen are dropped, so an API that shifts under you (new items pushing old ones into the next page) never produces duplicate rows. Eight pages in a row that add nothing new end the list, to guard against a cursor that never ends.
- Every load takes a generation number. A refresh, a retry or leaving the screen cancels the load in flight and starts a new generation, and any response from an older one is dropped, so a slow page can never overwrite fresher rows. A load cancelled by disappearing resumes when the list appears again. Throwing `CancellationError` or `URLError.cancelled` is never shown as an error.
- States: pulsing skeleton rows while the first page loads (pass `placeholder:` to render your own row redacted instead), a footer spinner while more loads, a full error view with a Try again block if the first page fails, an inline "Couldn't load more" chip with a solid Retry block that keeps every loaded row, and a quiet "You're all caught up" footer at the end (`endMessage: nil` hides it).
- Empty: the built-in state is a short message. Pass `empty:` for your own view, for example `ContentUnavailableView("No receipts", systemImage: "doc.text")`.
- Pull to refresh reloads from the first page and replaces the rows only when it succeeds. If it fails, the old rows stay and a "Couldn't refresh" chip with Retry appears above them.
- `layout: .list` (default) is a plain `List`, so swipe actions and row modifiers work in your row. `layout: .plain` uses a `LazyVStack` in a `ScrollView` with `Style.rowSpacing` and `Style.contentPadding`. Appending pages never moves the scroll position in either.
- To restart with new parameters, such as a search query or filter, give the list `.id(query)`.
- Concurrency: state lives on the main actor; `load` is a `@Sendable` async closure that runs off it. Items must be `Identifiable & Sendable`.
- `Style` (`PagedListStyle`): `text`, `secondaryText`, `field`, `error`, `retry`, `end`, `ink`, `rowSpacing`, `contentPadding`, `skeletonRows`. Skeleton and badge sizes scale with Dynamic Type, and the error chip stacks its Retry block under the message at large sizes.
- VoiceOver: "Loaded 20 more" is announced when a page appends, and each error is announced. The skeleton reads as a single "Loading" element, the spinner as "Loading more", and Retry is a button with a hint.
- Reduce Motion: the skeleton stops pulsing, the spinner becomes three fading dots, and chips crossfade instead of scaling in. A light haptic plays on Retry; routine loads are silent.

## Status Timeline (`StatusTimeline`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/lists/status-timeline
Category: Lists. iOS 17.0+.
Files: StatusTimeline.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add StatusTimeline

A vertical status timeline where the live step becomes a solid color block, connectors draw in as steps complete, nodes morph from number to check, the current node breathes, and any step expands to show its detail.

Vertical timeline for order tracking, delivery, or verification flows.

### Notes

- The live step is the graphic idea: its content becomes a solid block (`style.current`, tangerine) with dark ink, and its node matches with a breathing ring. Completed nodes are sage blocks with a drawn check, pending nodes are quiet numbered rings, and a failed step turns into a signal block with an x.
- Layout is nodes leading, content trailing: a 44pt column holds the 30pt node and the connector below it, which stretches to the row's own height, so long titles and expanded detail never break the line. Rows hug their content, so the timeline never stretches to fill a tall container.
- Connectors are trimmed paths: when a step becomes `.complete`, its connector draws downward in the text color over 0.45s and the node morphs from number to check with a `.success` haptic. After a `.failed` step the connector turns dashed with an `.error` haptic, so the trail visibly stops.
- Tap any step with `detail` to expand it; one step is expanded at a time. `expandsCurrent` opens the current step on appearance and follows it as the live step moves on. Detail on a block reads in ink; detail on other steps sits on a small `style.surface` card.
- `Style` (`StatusTimeline.Style`): `current`, `complete`, `failed`, `ink`, `text`, `muted`, `surface`. `tint:` still overrides both the current and complete colors.
- Reduce Motion replaces the breathing ring with a static halo and swaps the springs for short fades. Each step is a single VoiceOver element that reads its title, timestamp and status, and is a button only when it has detail.

### Parameters

- `steps`: Steps in order, each with a title, optional detail and timestamp, and a status.
- `tint`: Block color for the current step and completed nodes. `nil` uses `style.current` and `style.complete`.
- `expandsCurrent`: Start with the current step expanded.
- `style`: Block colors, text colors, connector and surface. Defaults to the house palette.

## Swipe Action Row (`SwipeActionRow`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/lists/swipe-action-row
Category: Lists. iOS 17.0+.
Files: SwipeActionRow.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add SwipeActionRow

Wraps any row in a soft card with swipe actions drawn as solid color blocks. Tiles grow in as the row opens, the drag rubber-bands, a full swipe arms with a haptic and lets the edge block take the whole bar, and a shared binding keeps one row open at a time.

Row with swipe-to-reveal actions that works in a plain `VStack` or `ScrollView`, not only in `List`.

### Notes

- Rows are soft cards (`style.surface`, 26pt continuous radius) and actions are solid color blocks with dark ink, separated from the card and each other by `style.tileGap`. Pass light block colors as `tint`; the house defaults are sky, butter, sage, tangerine and lilac, with signal (`#FF5B3A`) reserved for the one destructive or primary action.
- Drags are only claimed when they start horizontally, so the enclosing `ScrollView` keeps vertical scrolling. The card lifts off the tiles with a soft shadow as it opens, and the row clips sideways only so that shadow is never cut.
- Tiles grow in: the glyph scales from 55% to full size with the reveal and the label fades in over the last half, so a short peek never shows cropped text. Tiles dip to 94% when pressed. A full swipe (past 60% of the row width) lets the edge block take the whole bar, bounces its glyph, fires a rigid impact at the moment it arms, and runs that action on release. The first declared action sits at the screen edge, matching `.swipeActions`.
- Pass the same `open:` binding to every row in a list (with a unique `id:` per row) and only one row can be open at a time. Set the binding to `nil` to close all rows, or to a row's id to reveal its trailing actions (leading when there are none).
- Swiping toward an edge with no actions rubber-bands to a 40pt limit and springs back.
- `Style` (`SwipeActionRow.Style`, also `SwipeActionRowStyle`): `surface`, `tileInk`, `cornerRadius`, `tileWidth`, `tileGap`. `background:` still overrides the card fill; set `cornerRadius` and `tileGap` to 0 for classic full-bleed list rows.
- Reduce Motion keeps every state change but replaces the springs and the tile grow-in with short fades. All actions are exposed as VoiceOver custom actions on the row.
- Need grouped activity with categorize, split and expanding detail? That is the Transaction Row screen in Swift Pieces Pro.

### Parameters

- `id`: Identity used with `open`. Defaults to a private id, which still lets a parent close the row.
- `leading`: Actions revealed by swiping right. The first one sits at the edge and fires on a full swipe.
- `trailing`: Actions revealed by swiping left. The first one sits at the edge and fires on a full swipe.
- `background`: Opaque surface of the row card, which covers the tiles when closed. `nil` uses `style.surface`.
- `open`: Shared binding to the id of the open row. Swiping a row stores its id here and closes every other row bound to it; set it to `nil` to close all, or to a row id to reveal that row's trailing actions.
- `style`: Card surface, corner radius, tile ink, tile width and gap. Defaults to the house palette.
- `content`: Row content.

## Task Row (`TaskRow`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/lists/task-row
Category: Lists. iOS 17.0+.
Files: TaskRow.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add TaskRow

A task card whose check draws itself while the card flashes into a solid color block, a priority label block, a swipe-right that completes with a strike-through then compacts the row, swipe-left snooze and delete blocks, and a long-press lift that reports reorder moves.

Interactive task row for to-do lists, driven by a bound `Status`.

### Notes

- Rows are soft cards (`style.surface`, 22pt radius). Priority shows as a small HIGH, MED or LOW label block (tangerine, butter, sky) with dark ink; due dates carry a clock glyph; a snoozed task gets a lilac Snoozed label and a lilac check.
- Completion is a sequence, not a toggle: the card flashes into the solid `tint` block (sage by default) while the check draws in with a trimmed path and a `.success` haptic, the strike-through grows across the title, then the row settles back and compacts (smaller padding and type, due label and priority fold away). Setting `status` to `.completed` from outside runs the same sequence; rows that load already completed start settled. `.open` reverses it. Reduce Motion crossfades every step at once.
- Swipe right to the 104pt detent to complete (or reopen a completed row). The complete block's glyph grows with the reveal, the drag rubber-bands past the detent, and a rigid impact marks the moment it arms. Swipe left reveals Snooze (lilac) and Delete (signal) blocks, only for the callbacks you pass. Blocks and the check dip when pressed.
- Long-press (0.35s) lifts the row with a soft impact, scale 1.03 and a shadow; drag it vertically and `onMove` receives the number of row slots moved on release (negative is up). The gesture is only installed when `onMove` is set.
- `.disabled(true)` dims the row to 50% and turns off the swipe and lift.
- `Style` (`TaskRow.Style`): `surface`, `text`, `muted`, `ink`, `complete`, `snooze`, `delete`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `cornerRadius`. `tint:` still overrides the complete color.
- Stack rows with 8pt spacing on the ground. VoiceOver reads the row as one button with status, due date and priority, and exposes Complete/Reopen, Snooze, Delete and Move up/down as custom actions.
- Need grouped-by-day activity with split and expanding detail? That is the Transaction Row screen in Swift Pieces Pro.

### Parameters

- `title`: Task text.
- `status`: `.open`, `.completed`, or `.snoozed`. Set it from outside and the row animates to match.
- `due`: Optional secondary label, such as "Today, 5 PM".
- `priority`: Optional priority label block at the trailing edge.
- `tint`: Block color for the check, the completion flash and the complete tile. `nil` uses `style.complete`.
- `style`: Card surface, text colors, priority and tile blocks, and corner radius. Defaults to the house palette.
- `onTap`: Called when the row body is tapped, typically to open the task.
- `onSnooze`: Adds a Snooze block behind a left swipe and is called when it is chosen.
- `onDelete`: Adds a Delete block behind a left swipe and is called when it is chosen.
- `onMove`: Enables long-press lift and reports how many rows the user dragged it (negative is up) on release.

## Photo Viewer (`PhotoViewer`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/media/photo-viewer
Category: Media. iOS 17.0+.
Files: PhotoViewer.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add PhotoViewer

A full-screen photo surface with anchor-correct pinch zoom, momentum panning that decelerates into the bounds, double-tap zoom about the tap, paging between images, and pinch-out or drag-down to dismiss with a fading scrim. A close button and a page counter that turns into a live zoom readout float above, and a single tap hides them.

Photos-style viewer: page horizontally at rest, zoom and pan a page, pinch past the minimum or drag vertically to dismiss.

### Notes

- Zoom is anchored to the pinch start and to a double tap, so the content under the fingers stays put. Past `maxScale` the pinch rubber-bands with a rigid tick; releasing springs back. Returning to `minScale` plays a soft tick.
- A released pan coasts to `predictedEndTranslation`, clamped to the scaled bounds, with a duration that scales with the distance, so a flick decelerates into the edge instead of stopping dead.
- At rest a page ignores horizontal drags so the paging `ScrollView` handles them; vertical drags and any drag during a pinch belong to the dismiss. Paging is disabled while zoomed or dismissing.
- Two dismiss paths: drag vertically past 140 pt (or flick past a projected 280 pt) and the page flies off along the release direction; pinch below 80% of `minScale` and release. Both fade the scrim with progress and call `onDismiss` when the animation is logically complete.
- Reduce Motion shortens every settle to 0.2 s. VoiceOver gets Zoom in, Reset zoom, and the escape gesture dismisses.
- **v2:** floating chrome. A 44 pt close button (shown when `onDismiss` is set) fades the viewer out and calls `onDismiss`; a counter reads "2 / 3" at rest and turns into a light zoom readout ("2.5×") while zoomed. A single tap hides or shows the chrome, and the chrome fades as a dismiss drag progresses.
- `style:` (`PhotoViewer.Style`) sets `scrim` (near-black #121212), `chromeFill`, `chromeInk`, `zoomFill`, `zoomInk`, `showsCloseButton`, and `showsCounter`. `.bare` draws photos only.
- The example pages through flat color prints; a dismiss collapses the viewer and the example presents it again, so the preview only ever shows the viewer.
- For a full gallery screen, see the Pro Gallery screen (`depth-gallery`).

### Parameters

- `items`: The photos to page through. One item disables paging.
- `selection`: Optional binding to the visible item's id.
- `minScale`: Resting scale of a page.
- `maxScale`: Largest committed zoom; pinching past it rubber-bands, ticks, and springs back.
- `style`: Scrim and chrome. `.standard` draws a near-black scrim, a close button when `onDismiss` is set, and a counter that reads "2 / 5" at rest and the zoom level while zoomed.
- `onDismiss`: Called once a dismiss gesture or the close button has finished animating; end the presentation here.
- `content`: The photo for an item, typically a resizable image with `.scaledToFit()`.

## Story Strip (`StoryStrip`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/media/story-strip
Category: Media. iOS 17.0+.
Files: StoryStrip.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add StoryStrip

A Stories-style segment strip with a built-in clock that advances segments on a duration, a long-press hold that freezes the strip and shows a paused badge, tap zones for back and forward that answer with a chevron, and a manual progress mode when you own the timing.

Segment strip plus the gesture surface of a story player. Pass `duration` to let it run itself, or leave it nil and drive `progress`.

### Notes

- With `duration` set the strip runs itself: a `TimelineView(.animation)` draws the fill and a task sleeps for the rest of the segment, then advances `current`. Pausing (a hold, or `isPaused`) records the pause time and shifts the segment start on resume, so the fill continues exactly where it stopped.
- Without `duration` the strip is stateless like before: you own `current` and `progress`, and steps animate with a short linear curve so 30 Hz updates read as continuous.
- Holding anywhere on the surface for 200 ms freezes and dims the strip with a soft tick; releasing resumes. A shorter touch is a tap: the left 30% goes back (restarting the first segment) and the rest advances. Segment changes snap with `.snappy` and a `.selection` tick.
- `fillsContainer` stretches the invisible surface over the whole story with the bars pinned to the top; set it to false to use only the bar row.
- `onFinish` fires once when the last segment completes. VoiceOver reads "3 of 5", swipes up or down move between segments, and a custom action pauses or resumes.
- **v2:** holding shows a "Paused" badge under the trailing end of the bars, and a tap that moves back or forward flashes a chevron in that zone. Bars are 4 pt by default.
- `style:` (`StoryStrip.Style`) sets `barHeight`, `spacing`, `trackOpacity`, `inset`, `showsPausedBadge`, `showsTapHints`, and `ink` (the glyph color on `tint`). `.minimal` restores the version 1 look.
- The example runs the strip in dark ink over solid color slides with one big idea each.

### Parameters

- `count`: Number of segments.
- `current`: Index of the segment currently filling. The strip advances it when it drives the clock.
- `progress`: Fill of the current segment from 0 to 1, used only when `duration` is nil.
- `duration`: Seconds per segment. When set, a `TimelineView` clock fills the segment and advances at the end.
- `isPaused`: Optional external pause, for example while a reply sheet is up. Holding the strip pauses on its own.
- `tint`: Segment color; the track is the same color at low opacity.
- `style`: Bar geometry, track strength, and the paused badge and tap hints. `.standard` draws 4 pt bars and shows both.
- `fillsContainer`: Expand the gesture surface to the whole container so holds and taps work over the story, with the bars pinned to the top.
- `onFinish`: Called when the last segment completes.

## Drag to Dismiss (`DragToDismiss`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/motion/drag-to-dismiss
Category: Motion. iOS 17.0+.
Files: DragToDismiss.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add DragToDismiss

A modifier that lets a photo, card, or sheet follow a two-axis drag, rounds and shrinks it with progress over a styled scrim, reports its phase so the UI can say "release to close", then springs back or flies off along the drag vector past a distance or velocity threshold.

Photos-style dismiss: drag in any direction, the view rounds and shrinks as it travels, the scrim thins, and a far enough drag or a fast flick sends it off screen along the direction it was moving.

### Notes

- Apply it to the full-size root of a sheet or full-screen cover, or to a card wrapped in `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)`, so the scrim covers the screen while only the content moves.
- Commit happens past `threshold` points of travel or when `predictedEndTranslation` projects past twice that. The fly-off follows the release direction, travels far enough to clear the container, and runs faster for faster flicks. `onDismiss` fires when the fly-off is logically complete.
- Scroll cooperation: a scroll view inside the content keeps priority until it is at its top. On iOS 18 the modifier watches the scroll view with `onScrollGeometryChange`; on iOS 17 feed it `scrollOffset` yourself. Upward drags at the top go to the scroll view, and the scroll view is disabled for the duration of a captured drag so it cannot bounce underneath.
- Bind `progress` and scale your presenter from 0.94 toward 1 with it for sheet-like depth.
- Phases run idle, dragging, armed (a rigid tick at the threshold), returning, committing. VoiceOver's escape gesture commits a downward dismiss. Reduce Motion keeps the scale at 1 and shortens the springs.
- `style:` sets the scrim (`#141414` at 0.5 by default, `.clear` for none) and the shrink at full progress. `phase:` binds the current phase so the UI can switch a "Drag to close" hint to "Release to close" when armed.
- The `#Preview` is the single card the modifier moves: a butter boarding pass, with the modifier's own scrim behind it.
- For a full gallery built around this gesture, see the Pro Gallery screen.

### Parameters

- `threshold`: Drag distance in points that arms the dismiss. A flick whose projected travel passes twice this commits from a shorter drag.
- `cornerRadius`: Corner radius the view reaches at full progress; it starts square so full-screen content keeps its edges at rest.
- `progress`: Optional binding that receives the dismiss progress (0 at rest, 1 armed) so the presenter can scale its background from 0.94 back to 1.
- `scrollOffset`: Vertical offset of a scroll view inside the content. The drag is only captured at 0. On iOS 18 the modifier observes the inner scroll view itself.
- `phase`: Optional binding that receives the current phase (idle, dragging, armed, returning, committing), for a "Release to close" hint or to dim chrome while dragging.
- `style`: Scrim color and opacity at rest, and how much the view shrinks at full progress. `.standard` is a near-black `#141414` scrim at 0.5 with a 0.15 shrink.
- `onDismiss`: Called once the view has flown off; end the presentation here.

## Floating Dock (`FloatingDock`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/navigation/floating-dock
Category: Navigation. iOS 17.0+. Liquid Glass on iOS 26 with a Material fallback.
Files: FloatingDock.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add FloatingDock

A floating dock on a solid surface where the selected item becomes a color block with its label, a drag across the dock lifts each item under the finger with a name bubble and commits on release, badges count in a signal pill, and the whole dock tucks away on scroll.

Floating bottom dock of 4–5 icon items with a solid block selection and a scrub-to-pick gesture.

### Notes

- The dock is a solid surface capsule with two soft shadows. The selected item becomes a color block (butter by default, or `tint`) with an ink icon and label; the others compact to icon-only 48 pt targets. The block moves between items with `matchedGeometryEffect` and the selected symbol bounces once.
- Touch and drag across the dock to pick: the item under the finger lifts 5 pt, scales to 114%, and shows its name in a bubble above the dock, with a `.selection` tick per item. Release commits with a soft impact. A touch that doesn't travel presses the item (92%) and selects it on release. The block itself never stretches toward the finger.
- Badges are signal pills with ink numbers and a ring cut out of the icon, rolling with `.numericText`; on the selected item the count moves inline after the label as an ink pill. Counts over 99 show "99+".
- `Style` sets `surface`, `indicator`, `selectedInk`, `inactive`, `badge`, and `usesGlass` (Liquid Glass on iOS 26, a material before it). Reduce Transparency always uses the solid surface.
- `scrollProgress` slides the dock 120 pt down and fades it; drive it from your scroll direction (0 while scrolling up, 1 while scrolling down) and it springs either way. Above 0.5 it is also hidden from VoiceOver.
- VoiceOver sees a tab bar container whose items are buttons with selected state and badge value; double-tap selects. Reduce Motion removes the lift and scale.
- A floating tab bar with a lens that tracks and stretches toward the finger ships in Swift Pieces Pro (`lens-tab-bar`).

### Parameters

- `items`: Dock items in order. Four or five work best.
- `selection`: Index of the selected item.
- `tint`: Fill of the selected item's block. Defaults to the style's indicator, a butter block.
- `scrollProgress`: 0 keeps the dock in place, 1 tucks it below the screen. Feed it a value derived from scroll direction to hide the dock while scrolling down.
- `style`: Surface, indicator, ink, and badge colors. Defaults to `.standard`, the house palette.

## Stretch Header (`StretchHeader`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/navigation/stretch-header
Category: Navigation. iOS 17.0+.
Files: StretchHeader.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add StretchHeader

A hero header for your own ScrollView and NavigationStack: a heavy display title and uppercase eyebrow over a solid block hero that stretches on overscroll, a title that shrinks toward the real navigation bar, a stat row that pins under the bar, and a solid bar that fades in.

Hero header placed at the top of scroll content, paired with `.stretchHeaderBar(title:progress:style:)` on the scroll view.

### Notes

- Two parts: `StretchHeader` goes first inside your `ScrollView` content, and `.stretchHeaderBar(title:progress:style:)` goes on the `ScrollView` inside a `NavigationStack`. Share one `@State` progress between them. The modifier hides the system bar background, extends the scroll view under the bar, and draws its own solid bar in the style's `surface`, fading in with progress and gaining a soft shadow instead of a hairline.
- The title is display type: heavy, tight, 40 pt and scaled with Dynamic Type, with an optional uppercase `eyebrow` above it. Overscroll stretches the hero upward and grows the title a touch; scrolling moves the hero at 70% speed and the title at 55%, shrinking it toward the bar, and the inline title fades in over the last 20% of the collapse. States: expanded, stretching, collapsing, collapsed.
- `Style`: `.standard` puts ink on a solid block hero with no scrim; `.overImage` uses a white title over a soft scrim for photos. Both set `surface`, the house ground behind the pinned row and the bar. Copy a style and change one property to customize.
- The `subtitle` row (stats, avatar, tabs) pins under the bar once the hero has scrolled past it and draws above the content that follows. Give it its own padding.
- Progress comes from `onScrollGeometryChange` on iOS 18 (fed through the modifier) and from the header's own position in the `.scrollView` coordinate space on iOS 17. A soft haptic marks a deep pull.
- Reduce Motion drops the title parallax and the hero lag but keeps the stretch and the collapse. The hero reads as one header element and is hidden from VoiceOver once collapsed, when the inline title takes over.
- A full settings screen built around a header like this ships in Swift Pieces Pro (`settings-screen`).

### Parameters

- `title`: Large display title over the hero; the same string fades into the navigation bar as it collapses.
- `height`: Resting hero height in points.
- `progress`: Written by the header: 0 while expanded, 1 once collapsed behind the bar. Pass the same state to `.stretchHeaderBar`.
- `eyebrow`: Optional small uppercase label above the title, such as a place or a category. Defaults to none.
- `style`: Title ink, scrim, and surface colors. `.standard` suits solid block heroes; use `.overImage` for photos. Defaults to `.standard`.
- `hero`: Hero content, typically a solid color block or a resizable image. It is sized to fill the header.
- `subtitle`: Optional row under the hero (stats, avatar, tabs) that pins beneath the bar once the hero has scrolled away.

## Tracking Tabs (`TrackingTabs`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/navigation/tracking-tabs
Category: Navigation. iOS 17.0+.
Files: TrackingTabs.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add TrackingTabs

Tabs over a paging ScrollView whose solid block indicator follows the pages through fractional scroll progress, with ink titles that fade in as the block passes, optional counts, a pressed state, and a selection tick on settle.

Tab bar with a scroll-linked block indicator driving horizontally paged content.

### Notes

- Pages live in a horizontal `ScrollView` with `.scrollTargetBehavior(.paging)` and `containerRelativeFrame`, so each page is exactly one container wide. `selection` is synced with `scrollPosition(id:)` in both directions: taps animate the scroll with the same spring the indicator uses.
- The indicator is a solid butter block positioned from fractional page progress (`contentOffset.x / containerSize.width` via `onScrollGeometryChange` on iOS 18, the page row's position in the `.scrollView` space on iOS 17), interpolated between measured title frames. It follows the pages mid-swipe instead of jumping on settle; it does not stretch.
- Each title is drawn twice, muted and ink, and crossfaded by how much of the block sits over it, so the text on the block always has ink contrast. Optional `counts` show a monospaced count after each title and roll with `.numericText`.
- States: resting, swiping (block between titles), pressed (the tapped title scales to 94%), settled with a `.selection` haptic.
- `Style` sets `track`, `indicator`, `title`, and `selectedTitle`; `.standard` is the house surface track with a butter block and ink.
- Titles are buttons with selected traits and their count as the value; 44 pt tall. Reduce Motion shortens the tap animation and removes the press scale.
- A floating tab bar with a lens that stretches toward the finger ships in Swift Pieces Pro (`lens-tab-bar`).

### Parameters

- `titles`: One title per page, in order.
- `selection`: Index of the settled page. Tapping a title and swiping the pages both update it.
- `counts`: Optional count per page shown after its title, such as open tasks. Pass an empty array to hide counts. Defaults to none.
- `style`: Track, indicator, and title colors. Defaults to `.standard`, the house palette with a butter indicator.
- `page`: Builds the page for a given index. Pages fill the container width.

## Confirm Sheet (`ConfirmSheet`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/sheets/confirm-sheet
Category: Sheets. iOS 17.0+.
Files: ConfirmSheet.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add ConfirmSheet

A confirmation card that presents as a height-fitted bottom sheet or, inline, as a floating card you can drag away, with a solid icon tile that bounces on present, a heavy headline, a loading primary action that lands on a success check before dismissing, and a warning haptic for destructive choices.

Presents a confirmation card as a bottom sheet, or inline as an overlay in the current hierarchy.

### Notes

- Sheet mode measures the card and uses `.presentationDetents([.height(...)])`, so the sheet is exactly as tall as the content at the current Dynamic Type size, with `Style.surface` as its background.
- Inline mode floats the card at the bottom of the view it is applied to, with a dimmed backdrop, drag-to-dismiss (down is free, up rubber-bands), and a rigid impact tick the moment a flick would commit. Apply it near the root so the backdrop covers the screen.
- `confirm` is async: the primary button swaps to a spinner and both buttons disable until it returns, then the tile turns into a sage check with a `.success` haptic and the card dismisses about half a second later.
- Destructive cards use a tangerine tile and the signal-colored primary button, and play `.warning` when they appear. Other cards use a sky tile and a solid label-colored button. The tile symbol bounces on every presentation.
- `Style` sets every color and the card radius (34pt by default).
- Under Reduce Motion the card crossfades instead of sliding, the bounce is skipped and the success beat is shorter.
- For a floating booking card with detents, see the Stay screen (glass sheet) in Swift Pieces Pro.

### Parameters

- `isPresented`: Shows the card while `true`. Confirming, cancelling, and dragging away set it back to `false`.
- `inline`: `true` overlays the card in place with a dimmed backdrop and a rubber-banded drag to dismiss; `false` uses `.sheet` sized to the card.
- `systemImage`: SF Symbol in the icon tile.
- `title`: Headline.
- `message`: Supporting copy under the title.
- `confirmTitle`: Primary button title.
- `cancelTitle`: Quiet secondary button title.
- `isDestructive`: Uses the destructive tile and the signal-colored primary button, and plays a `.warning` haptic on present.
- `style`: Colors and corner radius. Defaults to the Swift Pieces house palette, adapting to light and dark.
- `confirm`: Async handler for the primary button; the button shows a spinner until it returns, the tile turns into a check, then the card dismisses.

## Permission Sheet (`PermissionSheet`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/sheets/permission-sheet
Category: Sheets. iOS 17.0+.
Files: PermissionSheet.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add PermissionSheet

A pre-permission sheet with a solid icon tile that bounces on present and turns into a check when granted, a heavy left-aligned headline, benefit rows on their own color tiles that stagger in, a signal-colored request button that spins while the system asks, and a denied result that swaps the copy and routes the button to Settings.

Explains a permission, runs the real request, and reacts to the result.

### Notes

- Present it in a `.sheet` with `.presentationBackground(PermissionSheet.Style.standard.surface)`; it also works inline in any container. The tile symbol bounces on each presentation and benefit rows stagger in once, each on its own color tile.
- `request` is your real permission call (for example `UNUserNotificationCenter.requestAuthorization`). The signal-colored button spins until it returns; `true` turns the tile and button sage with a check and a `.success` haptic, then calls `onGranted` about a second later so you can dismiss.
- A denial crossfades the title and message through a blur, hides the benefit rows, turns the tile sand with a gear, plays `.warning`, and turns the button into a solid "Open Settings" via `UIApplication.openSettingsURLString`.
- `Style` sets the surface, labels, tiles, benefit tile colors, action color and tile radius.
- Under Reduce Motion rows appear immediately, the copy swap skips the blur and the bounce is skipped.
- For a full multi-step onboarding flow, see the Onboarding screen in Swift Pieces Pro.

### Parameters

- `systemImage`: SF Symbol shown in the icon tile.
- `title`: Headline.
- `message`: One or two sentences of context.
- `benefits`: Rows that stagger in below the message, each on its own color tile.
- `allowTitle`: Primary button title.
- `deniedTitle`: Headline shown after the request returns `false`.
- `deniedMessage`: Copy shown after a denial, above the "Open Settings" button.
- `style`: Colors and tile shape. Defaults to the Swift Pieces house palette, adapting to light and dark.
- `request`: Async permission request; return `true` when granted. The button spins until it returns.
- `onGranted`: Called about a second after a grant, once the tile has turned into a check. Dismiss the sheet here.
- `onSkip`: Secondary handler. Omit to hide the "Not now" button.

## Toast (`Toast`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/sheets/toast
Category: Sheets. iOS 17.0+.
Files: Toast.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add Toast

A single toast card with a solid color tile for its kind, a bold message with an optional detail line, a signal-colored action such as Undo, and a thin timer that pauses while touched; placed inside the safe area so it clears the Dynamic Island and rides above the keyboard.

Presents one transient toast on the top or bottom edge.

### Notes

- Single instance by design. Presenting again while visible does nothing.
- The toast is a solid card: ink in light mode, raised grey in dark mode. A color tile marks its kind (`.info` sky, `.success` sage, `.warning` butter, `.error` tangerine) and bounces on arrival with a matching haptic.
- `detail` adds a quieter second line. The action is a signal-colored capsule that flashes a check, runs the handler, then dismisses.
- The countdown is a `.task` on the toast and is cancelled the moment the toast leaves; touching the toast pauses it (the thin bar freezes and the card presses in) and releasing resumes from where it stopped. Swipe toward the edge to dismiss.
- Placement reads the safe area of the view it is applied to: at the top it clears the Dynamic Island, at the bottom it rises with the keyboard. Apply the modifier to a view that does not ignore safe areas.
- Colors live in `Toast.Appearance` (passed as `appearance:`), because `Toast.Style` already names the kind. The card is opaque, so it reads the same with Reduce Transparency.
- The message and detail are posted as a VoiceOver announcement on appear; the action button is a real button with its own label.
- For stacked, queued alerts with a notifications feed, see the Notifications screen (toast stack) in Swift Pieces Pro.

### Parameters

- `isPresented`: Shows the toast while `true`; the timer, swipe, and action set it back to `false`.
- `message`: Text to show, in bold. Keep it to one line.
- `detail`: Optional quieter second line, such as where the item went.
- `systemImage`: Optional SF Symbol; defaults to a symbol that matches `style`.
- `style`: The kind of toast, which picks the tile color and default symbol: `.info`, `.success`, `.warning`, or `.error`.
- `duration`: Seconds before it dismisses on its own. The countdown pauses while the toast is touched.
- `position`: `.top` or `.bottom` edge to slide in from.
- `action`: Optional trailing button (for example Undo). Tapping it flashes a check, runs the handler, then dismisses.
- `appearance`: Colors and corner radius. Defaults to the Swift Pieces house palette, adapting to light and dark.

## Expandable Text (`ExpandableText`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/text/expandable-text
Category: Text. iOS 17.0+.
Files: ExpandableText.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add ExpandableText

A paragraph clamped to a line limit that measures whether it is really truncated, and only then fades the end of its last line into a trailing "more" link; tapping grows the block smoothly to its full height with no reflow, a "less" link collapses it, links stay tappable, and VoiceOver always reads the whole text.

A "Read more" paragraph that shows `more` only when the text is actually truncated. SwiftUI cannot tell you whether a `Text` was truncated, so this measures three hidden copies at the real width: the full text, the text at `lineLimit` lines, and the text at one line fewer (which locates the last visible line). The copies re-measure on width, Dynamic Type and text changes. When the full height exceeds the limited height, the visible text is laid out in full and clipped to the limited height; the end of the last line fades out (a transparent mask, so it works over any background) and a `more` link sits in the faded space on the trailing edge. Expanding animates the clip to the full height, so lines never reflow or jump. Font and color come from the environment like `Text`: apply `.font(...)`, `.foregroundStyle(...)` and `.multilineTextAlignment(...)` to the piece. VoiceOver reads the full text in both states and gets "Show more" / "Show less" actions; the visual links are hidden from it.

### Notes

- SwiftUI has no API that reports truncation. The piece lays out three hidden copies at the paragraph's real width: the full text, the text at `lineLimit` lines, and the text at one line fewer. "More" appears only when the full height is taller than the clamped height, so a short text never shows it.
- The copies re-measure whenever the width, Dynamic Type size, font or text changes (`onGeometryChange` on iOS 18, a `GeometryReader` on iOS 17). They never read the expanded state, so there is no layout loop.
- Until the first measurement lands, a plain `lineLimit` Text shows the same first lines, so first appearance does not jump.
- Collapsed, the full text is clipped to the clamped height. The end of the last line fades to transparent through a mask and "more" sits in the faded space. The mask needs no background color, so it works over cards, images and materials. Set `Style.fade` to paint a gradient into a solid color instead.
- Expanding animates the clip height to the full height. Lines are laid out once at full length, so nothing reflows or jumps. "Less" fades in under the text on the trailing edge; `showsLess: false` keeps the paragraph open.
- Font, color and alignment come from the environment, like `Text`: `.font`, `.foregroundStyle`, `.multilineTextAlignment`.
- `AttributedString` keeps bold, italics and links. With `togglesOnTap`, tapping the body toggles too; a tap that opens a link does not toggle, and lines hidden below the fold have no hit area. Links open through your `openURL` environment action.
- `isExpanded` lets you drive or observe the state, for example to keep one review open at a time.
- RTL: the fade and "more" sit on the trailing side, which is the left in right-to-left languages.
- `Style` sets the link color, link weight, fade width (scaled with Dynamic Type) and the optional solid fade color. `.disabled(true)` dims the links and stops toggling.
- Reduce Motion: expanding and collapsing happen without animation.
- VoiceOver reads the full text in both states, with links in the rotor. "Show more" and "Show less" actions resize the paragraph for sighted VoiceOver users; the visual links are hidden from VoiceOver.
- The "more" and "less" links draw at one line tall but have a hit area of at least 44 by 44 points.

### Parameters

- `text`: The paragraph. A `String` is shown verbatim; an `AttributedString` keeps bold, italics and tappable links.
- `lineLimit`: Lines shown while collapsed. Values below 1 are treated as 1.
- `isExpanded`: Optional binding to drive or observe the state from outside. `nil` keeps the state internally.
- `moreLabel`: The trailing link on the last collapsed line. Localized from your app's strings; defaults to "more".
- `lessLabel`: The link under the expanded text. Localized from your app's strings; defaults to "less".
- `showsLess`: When false, an expanded paragraph stays expanded (no "less" link, and tapping the body does nothing).
- `togglesOnTap`: When true, tapping anywhere on the paragraph also expands or collapses it. Links inside the text still open.
- `style`: Link color and weight, fade width, and an optional solid fade color. Defaults to the house palette.

## Glass Text (`GlassText`)

URL: https://swiftpieces.com/docs/components/text/glass-text
Category: Text. iOS 17.0+. Liquid Glass on iOS 26 with a Material fallback.
Files: GlassText.swift
Install: npx swiftpieces add GlassText

Liquid Glass rendered on the actual glyph outlines of a string, one or several lines, with a specular Material fallback below iOS 26, a solid fill under Reduce Transparency and Dynamic Type scaling.

Liquid Glass applied to text outlines via Core Text glyph paths. The glyph path is built once per string and font, then handed to `glassEffect(_:in:)` as a shape. Split the string with `\n` for a stacked display title; lines use tight display leading.

### Notes
